Enable `verbatimModuleSyntax` for explicit import/export control.\n00006| - Always run build (`pnpm build`), tests (`pnpm test`), linter (`eslint --max-warnings 0`), and type-checker (`tsc --noEmit`) before finishing tasks.\n00007| - Use `pnpm` over `npm` for faster installs and strict dependency resolution. Run `pnpm audit` and `pnpm outdated` regularly to check for vulnerabilities.\n00008| - Configure `moduleResolution: \"bundler\"` or `\"node16\"` for Node.js projects. Use path aliases (`@/` for `src/`) in tsconfig and build config for clean imports.\n00009| - Use `tsx` for running TypeScript directly in development: `tsx src/index.ts`. Use `tsup` or `esbuild` for production builds (faster than tsc). Configure source maps for debugging.\n00010| - Enable `isolatedModules: true` for compatibility with fast transpilers. Avoid const enums and namespace merging patterns.\n00011| - Use ESLint 9+ with flat config (`eslint.config.js`). Enable `@typescript-eslint/strict-type-checked` ruleset for backend code. Use Biome as faster alternative.\n00012| - For monorepos, use pnpm workspaces with `workspace:*` protocol. Use Turborepo for build orchestration and caching. Structure as: `apps/`, `packages/`, `services/`.\n00013| - Pin Node.js version with `.nvmrc` or `package.json` engines field. Use LTS versions (20.x or 22.x). Use Docker for consistent environments: `FROM node:22-alpine`.\n00014| - Configure TypeScript with `skipLibCheck: true` for faster builds, `esModuleInterop: true` for CJS compatibility, `resolveJsonModule: true` for importing JSON configs.\n00015| \n00016| ## Error Handling\n00017| \n00018| - Never throw raw strings or objects. Always throw Error instances with codes: `throw new AppError('USER_NOT_FOUND', 'User not found', { userId })`. Include error codes for client handling.\n00019| - Use discriminated unions for Result types in business logic: `type Result<T, E = Error> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: E }`. Prefer over throwing in pure functions.\n00020| - Implement custom error hierarchy extending Error: `class ValidationError extends Error { constructor(message: string, public readonly field: string, public readonly code: string) { super(message); this.name = 'ValidationError'; Error.captureStackTrace(this, this.constructor); } }`.\n00021| - Define domain-specific error types: `class DatabaseError`, `class AuthenticationError`, `class RateLimitError`. Include metadata for debugging: timestamp, request ID, user context.\n00022| - Use `cause` property for error chaining (Node 16.9+): `throw new Error('Failed to create user', { cause: originalError })`. Preserves full error context through stack.\n00023| - Implement global error handler middleware: Catch all errors, log with context, return sanitized responses. Never expose internal errors to clients: `{ code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', message: 'An error occurred' }`.\n00024| - For HTTP APIs, map errors to status codes consistently: 400 (validation), 401 (auth), 403 (forbidden), 404 (not found), 409 (conflict), 429 (rate limit), 500 (internal). Use custom error mapper.\n00025| - Validate external data at API boundaries with Zod schemas. Transform Zod errors into structured responses: `{ code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR', message: string, details: { field: string, message: string }[] }`.\n00026| - Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient failures (database deadlocks, external APIs). Use `p-retry` library with jitter: `retry(() => fetchData(), { retries: 3, factor: 2 })`.\n00027| - Use `never` return type for assertion functions: `function assertAuthenticated(user: User | null): asserts user is User { if (!user) throw new AuthError() }`. Narrows types after assertion.\n00028| \n00029| ## Async & Concurrency\n00030| \n00031| - Always use `async/await` over raw Promises. Use `Promise.all()` for parallel execution: `const [users, posts] = await Promise.all([db.users.findMany(), db.posts.findMany()])`. Never sequential awaits for independent operations.\n00032| - Use `Promise.allSettled()` when you need all results regardless of failures. Use `Promise.race()` for timeout patterns: `Promise.race([fetchData(), timeout(5000)])`.\n00033| - Implement proper cancellation with AbortController for HTTP requests, database queries: `const controller = new AbortController(); fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal }); setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 5000)`.\n00034| - Use message queues (BullMQ, Bee-Queue) for background jobs and async processing. Define typed job payloads: `type EmailJob = { type: 'email'; to: string; template: string; data: Record<string, unknown> }`. Implement job retry and dead-letter queues.\n00035| - Organize system into subsystems using message-passing architecture. Use EventEmitter or custom event bus for internal events. For complex workflows, use state machines with XState.\n00036| - For CPU-intensive tasks, use worker threads (`node:worker_threads`). Communicate via `postMessage()` with typed messages. Use Piscina for worker pool management. Never block event loop.\n00037| - Avoid shared state between requests. Use request-scoped context with AsyncLocalStorage: `const requestContext = new AsyncLocalStorage<{ requestId: string; userId?: string }>()`. Access in nested functions without passing explicitly.\n00038| - Implement graceful shutdown: Listen for SIGTERM/SIGINT, stop accepting new connections, drain active requests, close database connections, flush logs. Use `@fastify/graceful-shutdown` or custom implementation.\n00039| - Use streaming for large payloads: Node.js streams, async iterators. Process data in chunks to avoid memory issues: `for await (const chunk of readStream) { await processChunk(chunk) }`.\n00040| - Handle uncaught errors: `process.on('uncaughtException')`, `process.on('unhandledRejection')`. Log error, clean up resources, gracefully exit. Use process managers (PM2, Kubernetes) for restart.\n00041| - Use connection pooling for databases (Prisma, TypeORM), Redis, HTTP clients. Configure pool size based on workload: Start with `max: 10`, tune based on monitoring.\n00042| - Implement circuit breakers for external dependencies using `opossum`. Open circuit after threshold failures, prevent cascading failures. Use fallback responses during circuit open.\n00043| \n00044| ## Type Design & API\n00045| \n00046| - Use `interface` for object shapes that might be extended (DTOs, entities). Use `type` for unions, intersections, mapped types. Prefer `interface` for public APIs (better error messages).\n00047| - Define API request/response types separately from domain models: `type CreateUserRequest = { email: string; name: string }`, `type UserResponse = { id: string; email: string; name: string; createdAt: string }`. Never expose internal models directly.\n00048| - Use branded types for domain primitives: `type UserId = string & { readonly __brand: 'UserId' }; const makeUserId = (id: string): UserId => id as UserId`. Prevents mixing email with userId.\n00049| - Use Zod for runtime validation and type inference: `const CreateUserSchema = z.object({ email: z.string().email(), name: z.string().min(1) }); type CreateUserDto = z.infer<typeof CreateUserSchema>`. Single source of truth.\n00050| - Implement discriminated unions for polymorphic APIs: `type Event = { type: 'user.created'; userId: string } | { type: 'post.published'; postId: string }`. Use in event handlers, message queues.\n00051| - Use template literal types for API routes: `type HttpMethod = 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'DELETE'; type ApiRoute = \\`/api/\\${string}\\`; type Endpoint<M extends HttpMethod> = { method: M; path: ApiRoute }`.\n00052| - Define service interfaces with dependency injection in mind: `interface UserService { createUser(dto: CreateUserDto): Promise<User>; findById(id: UserId): Promise<User | null> }`. Easy to mock, test, replace implementations.\n00053| - Use generic constraints for type-safe query builders: `function where<T, K extends keyof T>(field: K, value: T[K]): Query<T>`. Ensures field exists and value matches type.\n00054| - Use utility types extensively: `Omit<User, 'password'>` for public user type, `Partial<User>` for update DTOs, `Pick<User, 'id' | 'email'>` for minimal representations.\n00055| - Implement builder pattern for complex objects: `class QueryBuilder<T> { where(field: keyof T, value: unknown): this; orderBy(field: keyof T): this; build(): Query<T> }`. Store tokens in httpOnly, secure, SameSite=Strict cookies. For APIs, use Authorization header: `Bearer <token>`. Validate signature and expiration.\n- Use bcrypt or argon2 for password hashing. Never store plain text passwords. Use high cost factor: `bcrypt.hash(password, 12)` or `argon2.hash(password, { timeCost: 3, memoryCost: 65536 })`.\n- Implement CSRF protection for state-changing operations. Use SameSite cookies or CSRF tokens. For Express, use `csurf` middleware. For Fastify, use `@fastify/csrf-protection`.\n- Configure CORS properly: Allow only trusted origins. Never use `*` with credentials. Set specific origins: `{ origin: ['https://app.example.com'], credentials: true }`. Use `cors` middleware.\n- Implement rate limiting per IP and per user. Use Redis-backed rate limiters: `express-rate-limit` with Redis store, or `@fastify/rate-limit`. Apply different limits to sensitive endpoints (login, signup).\n- Prevent injection attacks: Use parameterized queries for SQL (never string concatenation). Use ORM query builders (Prisma, TypeORM). Validate input against allowlist patterns.\n- Sanitize output for logs and responses. Never log passwords, tokens, credit cards. Implement redaction: `logger.info({ user: redact(user, ['password', 'ssn']) })`. Use `fast-redact` library.\n- Implement Content Security Policy for served HTML: `helmet` middleware sets security headers. Configure CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options.\n- Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual()` for comparing secrets (tokens, signatures). Prevents timing attacks. For crypto operations, use `node:crypto` module, never custom implementations.\n- Implement secure session management: Rotate session IDs after login. Expire sessions after inactivity. Store sessions in Redis with TTL. Use `express-session` or `@fastify/secure-session`.\n- Validate file uploads: Check file type (magic bytes, not extension), size limits, scan for malware. Store uploads outside web root. Use signed URLs for access (S3, CloudFront).\n- Audit dependencies with `pnpm audit`, `npm audit`, or Socket.dev. Enable Dependabot/Renovate. Review new dependencies for supply chain attacks. Use `socket npm install` for security analysis.\n- Implement security headers: Use `helmet` middleware. Enable HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin.\n\n## Serialization & Data\n\n- Use Zod for runtime validation of API requests and external data: `const parsed = CreateUserSchema.parse(req.body)`. Throws on validation failure with detailed errors.\n- Transform Zod validation errors into user-friendly API responses: `.safeParse()` returns Result type. Map errors: `error.issues.map(i => ({ field: i.path.join('.'), message: i.message }))`.\n- Serialize dates as ISO 8601 strings in JSON responses: `JSON.stringify({ createdAt: new Date().toISOString() })`. Define serializers for custom types: Use `superjson` for Date, Map, Set, BigInt, RegExp.\n- Implement DTO transformers: Map database models to API responses. Exclude sensitive fields (password, internal IDs). Use class-transformer or manual mappers: `function toUserResponse(user: User): UserResponse { return { id: user.id, email: user.email } }`.\n- Use Prisma for type-safe database access. Define schema in `schema.prisma`, generate types with `prisma generate`. Use relations, transactions, middleware for business logic.\n- Implement database migrations: Use Prisma Migrate, TypeORM migrations, or Knex. Version migrations, test rollbacks. Never modify production schema manually.\n- Handle pagination with cursor-based approach for large datasets: `{ data: T[], nextCursor: string | null, hasMore: boolean }`. Encode cursor: `Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({ id, createdAt })).toString('base64')`.\n- Use JSON Schema for API documentation and validation. Generate types from schema with `json-schema-to-typescript`. Or use Zod and generate JSON Schema: `zodToJsonSchema()`.\n- Implement ETags for cache validation: Hash response body, set ETag header. Check `If-None-Match`, return 304 if match. Use `etag` middleware or custom implementation.\n- Use Protocol Buffers for gRPC services or binary APIs. Define `.proto` schemas, generate TypeScript types with `ts-proto`. Smaller payloads, faster serialization than JSON.\n- Handle BigInt serialization: JSON.stringify doesn't support BigInt. Use custom replacer: `JSON.stringify(obj, (key, value) => typeof value === 'bigint' ? value.toString() : value)` or use `json-bigint` library.\n- Implement database query result caching: Use Redis for frequently accessed data. Define TTL per entity type. Invalidate on updates: `await redis.del(\\`user:\\${userId}\\`)`.\n\n## Testing\n\n- Use Vitest over Jest for modern projects (faster, native ESM, better TypeScript support). Configure with `vitest.config.ts`. Run with `vitest run` for CI, `vitest watch` for development.\n- Write unit tests colocated with code: `userService.test.ts` next to `userService.ts`. Use descriptive test names: `it('should throw ValidationError when email is invalid', async () => {})`. Follow AAA pattern.\n- Write integration tests in `tests/integration/`. Test API endpoints end-to-end with real database (use test database). Use supertest or native fetch: `const response = await fetch('http://localhost:3000/api/users', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(data) })`.\n- Use test fixtures for database data: Create factory functions: `function createUser(overrides?: Partial<User>): Promise<User>`. Use `@faker-js/faker` for generating realistic test data.\n- Mock external dependencies (third-party APIs, email services) with MSW (Mock Service Worker) for HTTP or `vi.mock()` for modules. Test error scenarios: network failures, timeouts, rate limits.\n- Test database interactions with test containers (Testcontainers) or in-memory databases (better-sqlite3). Isolate tests: Clear database between tests or use transactions: `beforeEach(async () => { await db.truncate() })`.\n- Test authentication and authorization: Mock auth tokens, test protected endpoints return 401/403. Test role-based access: `it('should return 403 when user lacks admin role', async () => {})`.\n- Test error handling explicitly: Verify error codes, status codes, error messages. Use `expect().rejects.toThrow()` for async errors. Test validation errors return proper structure.\n- Use snapshot tests sparingly (only for complex responses). Prefer explicit assertions: `expect(response.status).toBe(200); expect(response.body).toMatchObject({ id: expect.any(String), email: 'test@example.com' })`.\n- Implement E2E tests with Playwright for critical user flows. Test across different databases, environments. Run in CI with Docker Compose: database, Redis, app.\n- Aim for 80%+ coverage on business logic. Use `v8` coverage in Vitest: `vitest --coverage`. Generate reports: `--reporter=html`. Focus on critical paths: auth, payments, data mutations.\n- Test concurrency issues: Race conditions, deadlocks. Use Promise.all to trigger parallel operations: `await Promise.all([updateUser(1), updateUser(1)])`. Verify proper locking or optimistic locking.\n\n## Logging & Observability\n\n- Use Pino for structured logging (fastest JSON logger for Node.js). Configure with `pino({ level: process.env.LOG_LEVEL || 'info', formatters: { level: (label) => ({ level: label }) } })`. Use pretty printing in dev: `pino-pretty`.\n- Implement different log levels: `fatal` for crashes, `error` for errors requiring attention, `warn` for degraded state, `info` for important events (API calls, user actions), `debug` and `trace` for diagnostics.\n- Add request context to all logs: request ID, user ID, session ID. Use AsyncLocalStorage to propagate context: `const storage = new AsyncLocalStorage<Context>()`. Create middleware to inject context: `req.log = logger.child({ requestId: uuid(), userId: req.user?.id })`.\n- Log structured data with fields: `logger.info({ userId, action: 'user.created', duration: 123 }, 'User created successfully')`. Enables querying logs by fields. Never concatenate strings: `logger.info('User ' + id)`.\n- Integrate error tracking with Sentry, Bugsnag, or Rollbar. Initialize with DSN: `Sentry.init({ dsn: process.env.SENTRY_DSN, environment: process.env.NODE_ENV })`. Capture errors: `Sentry.captureException(error)`. Set context: `Sentry.setUser()`, `Sentry.setTag()`.\n- Implement distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry. Instrument with auto-instrumentation: `@opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node`. Export traces to Jaeger, Zipkin, Datadog, New Relic. Add custom spans for business logic.\n- Log all API requests/responses in development. Redact sensitive data (tokens, passwords, SSN) in production logs. Use `fast-redact` or custom redaction: `logger.child({ redact: ['password', 'token'] })`.\n- Monitor application metrics: Request rate, error rate, latency (p50, p95, p99), active connections. Use Prometheus with `prom-client`: `const httpRequestDuration = new Histogram({ name: 'http_request_duration_seconds', help: 'Duration of HTTP requests in seconds' })`.\n- Implement health checks: `/health` endpoint returning 200 when healthy. Check database connectivity, Redis, external dependencies. Use for load balancer health checks, Kubernetes liveness/readiness probes.\n- Set up alerting: Error rate spikes, high latency, failed health checks. Use PagerDuty, Opsgenie, or cloud provider alerts. Define SLOs and alert on SLO violations.\n- Use structured logs for audit trail: Log all state-changing operations (create, update, delete) with actor, timestamp, old/new values. Store in separate audit log table or log aggregation service.\n- Collect and analyze metrics: Use Datadog, New Relic, Prometheus + Grafana. Track business metrics (signups, orders, revenue) alongside technical metrics. Create dashboards for observability.\n\n## Performance\n\n- Profile before optimizing: Use Node.js built-in profiler (`node --prof`), Chrome DevTools (inspect mode), or `clinic.js` for flame graphs, heap analysis, event loop analysis.\n- Optimize database queries: Use indexes on frequently queried fields. Avoid N+1 queries (use joins or dataloader). Use `EXPLAIN` to analyze query plans. Add pagination to large result sets.\n- Implement caching strategy: Cache frequently accessed data in Redis with TTL. Use cache-aside pattern: Check cache, miss → fetch from DB → set cache. Define cache key convention: `entity:id`.\n- Use connection pooling: Configure database pool size based on workload. For Prisma: `connection_limit` in database URL. For Redis: `ioredis` with pool. Use `cluster` module to spawn workers per CPU core. Or deploy multiple instances behind load balancer (better for containers).\n- Optimize cold starts: Minimize startup work. Lazy load heavy dependencies. Use `import()` for conditional imports. For serverless (AWS Lambda), reduce bundle size, use provisioned concurrency.\n- Implement request coalescing: Deduplicate concurrent identical requests (e.g., same user requesting same resource multiple times). Avoid packages requiring manual type definitions.\n- Use workspace dependencies in monorepos: Define in `[workspace.dependencies]` in root package.json. Use `workspace:*` for internal packages. Never use `npm update` without testing.\n\n## Documentation\n\n- Write TSDoc comments for exported functions, classes, types: `/** Creates a new user. @param dto - User creation data. @returns Created user with generated ID. @throws {ValidationError} When email is invalid. @example \\`\\`\\`ts\\nawait createUser({ email: 'user@example.com', name: 'John' })\\n\\`\\`\\` */`.\n- Document API endpoints with OpenAPI/Swagger: Use `@fastify/swagger` or `swagger-jsdoc`. Host on `/docs` endpoint.\n- Document environment variables in `.env.example` with comments: `# Database connection string (required)\\nDATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/db`. Use template: Title, Status, Context, Decision, Consequences. Number sequentially: `001-use-postgresql-over-mongodb.md`.\n- Add inline comments for complex business logic only. Code should be self-documenting with clear names. Document table purposes, indexes, constraints. Explain complex queries or stored procedures. Use `prisma-docs` or `dbdocs.io`.\n\n## Code Style\n\n- Use functional programming principles: Pure functions, immutability, composition. Avoid mutations: Use `map/filter/reduce` over `for` loops modifying arrays. Use spread operator: `{ ...obj, key: newValue }`.\n- Follow naming conventions: `camelCase` for variables/functions, `PascalCase` for types/interfaces/classes, `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` for constants. Use descriptive names: `fetchUserById` not `getUser`.\n- Keep functions small and focused: <50 lines ideally. Single responsibility. Extract complex logic into well-named helper functions. Use early returns: `if (!user) return null;`.\n- Order imports consistently: Node.js built-ins first (`node:fs`, `node:path`), external dependencies second (alphabetically), internal modules third (`@/services/*`), types fourth. Use auto-sorting with `eslint-plugin-import`.\n- Use const by default, let only when reassignment needed. Never use var. Use destructuring: `const { id, email } = user` not `const id = user.id`.\n- Prefer arrow functions for callbacks and inline functions: `const double = (x: number) => x * 2`. Use function declarations for top-level exported functions, methods.\n- Use template literals for string interpolation: `` `User ${id} not found` `` not `'User ' + id + ' not found'`. Better for tree-shaking, refactoring. Use default exports sparingly (e.g., Express app).\n- Use trailing commas in multi-line arrays, objects, function parameters: Cleaner git diffs, easier to reorder lines. Use barrel exports (`index.ts`) for clean imports: `import { createUser, findUser } from '@/services/user'`.\n- Use async/await consistently. Never mix promises and callbacks. Handle errors with try/catch at boundaries. Use `.catch()` only when truly recovering from error, not for logging.\n- Prefer composition over inheritance. Use dependency injection for testability. Enable `verbatimModuleSyntax` for explicit import/export control.\n00006| - Always run build (`pnpm build`), tests (`pnpm test`), linter (`eslint --max-warnings 0`), and type-checker (`tsc --noEmit`) before finishing tasks.\n00007| - Use `pnpm` over `npm` for faster installs and strict dependency resolution. Run `pnpm audit` and `pnpm outdated` regularly to check for vulnerabilities.\n00008| - Configure `moduleResolution: \"bundler\"` or `\"node16\"` for Node.js projects. Use path aliases (`@/` for `src/`) in tsconfig and build config for clean imports.\n00009| - Use `tsx` for running TypeScript directly in development: `tsx src/index.ts`. Use `tsup` or `esbuild` for production builds (faster than tsc). Configure source maps for debugging.\n00010| - Enable `isolatedModules: true` for compatibility with fast transpilers. Avoid const enums and namespace merging patterns.\n00011| - Use ESLint 9+ with flat config (`eslint.config.js`). Enable `@typescript-eslint/strict-type-checked` ruleset for backend code. Use Biome as faster alternative.\n00012| - For monorepos, use pnpm workspaces with `workspace:*` protocol. Use Turborepo for build orchestration and caching. Structure as: `apps/`, `packages/`, `services/`.\n00013| - Pin Node.js version with `.nvmrc` or `package.json` engines field. Use LTS versions (20.x or 22.x). Use Docker for consistent environments: `FROM node:22-alpine`.\n00014| - Configure TypeScript with `skipLibCheck: true` for faster builds, `esModuleInterop: true` for CJS compatibility, `resolveJsonModule: true` for importing JSON configs.\n00015| \n00016| ## Error Handling\n00017| \n00018| - Never throw raw strings or objects. Always throw Error instances with codes: `throw new AppError('USER_NOT_FOUND', 'User not found', { userId })`. Include error codes for client handling.\n00019| - Use discriminated unions for Result types in business logic: `type Result<T, E = Error> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: E }`. Prefer over throwing in pure functions.\n00020| - Implement custom error hierarchy extending Error: `class ValidationError extends Error { constructor(message: string, public readonly field: string, public readonly code: string) { super(message); this.name = 'ValidationError'; Error.captureStackTrace(this, this.constructor); } }`.\n00021| - Define domain-specific error types: `class DatabaseError`, `class AuthenticationError`, `class RateLimitError`. Include metadata for debugging: timestamp, request ID, user context.\n00022| - Use `cause` property for error chaining (Node 16.9+): `throw new Error('Failed to create user', { cause: originalError })`. Preserves full error context through stack.\n00023| - Implement global error handler middleware: Catch all errors, log with context, return sanitized responses. Never expose internal errors to clients: `{ code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', message: 'An error occurred' }`.\n00024| - For HTTP APIs, map errors to status codes consistently: 400 (validation), 401 (auth), 403 (forbidden), 404 (not found), 409 (conflict), 429 (rate limit), 500 (internal). Use custom error mapper.\n00025| - Validate external data at API boundaries with Zod schemas. Transform Zod errors into structured responses: `{ code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR', message: string, details: { field: string, message: string }[] }`.\n00026| - Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient failures (database deadlocks, external APIs). Use `p-retry` library with jitter: `retry(() => fetchData(), { retries: 3, factor: 2 })`.\n00027| - Use `never` return type for assertion functions: `function assertAuthenticated(user: User | null): asserts user is User { if (!user) throw new AuthError() }`. Narrows types after assertion.\n00028| \n00029| ## Async & Concurrency\n00030| \n00031| - Always use `async/await` over raw Promises. Use `Promise.all()` for parallel execution: `const [users, posts] = await Promise.all([db.users.findMany(), db.posts.findMany()])`. Never sequential awaits for independent operations.\n00032| - Use `Promise.allSettled()` when you need all results regardless of failures. Use `Promise.race()` for timeout patterns: `Promise.race([fetchData(), timeout(5000)])`.\n00033| - Implement proper cancellation with AbortController for HTTP requests, database queries: `const controller = new AbortController(); fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal }); setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 5000)`.\n00034| - Use message queues (BullMQ, Bee-Queue) for background jobs and async processing. Define typed job payloads: `type EmailJob = { type: 'email'; to: string; template: string; data: Record<string, unknown> }`. Implement job retry and dead-letter queues.\n00035| - Organize system into subsystems using message-passing architecture. Use EventEmitter or custom event bus for internal events. For complex workflows, use state machines with XState.\n00036| - For CPU-intensive tasks, use worker threads (`node:worker_threads`). Communicate via `postMessage()` with typed messages. Use Piscina for worker pool management. Never block event loop.\n00037| - Avoid shared state between requests. Use request-scoped context with AsyncLocalStorage: `const requestContext = new AsyncLocalStorage<{ requestId: string; userId?: string }>()`. Access in nested functions without passing explicitly.\n00038| - Implement graceful shutdown: Listen for SIGTERM/SIGINT, stop accepting new connections, drain active requests, close database connections, flush logs. Use `@fastify/graceful-shutdown` or custom implementation.\n00039| - Use streaming for large payloads: Node.js streams, async iterators. Process data in chunks to avoid memory issues: `for await (const chunk of readStream) { await processChunk(chunk) }`.\n00040| - Handle uncaught errors: `process.on('uncaughtException')`, `process.on('unhandledRejection')`. Log error, clean up resources, gracefully exit. Use process managers (PM2, Kubernetes) for restart.\n00041| - Use connection pooling for databases (Prisma, TypeORM), Redis, HTTP clients. Configure pool size based on workload: Start with `max: 10`, tune based on monitoring.\n00042| - Implement circuit breakers for external dependencies using `opossum`. Open circuit after threshold failures, prevent cascading failures. Use fallback responses during circuit open.\n00043| \n00044| ## Type Design & API\n00045| \n00046| - Use `interface` for object shapes that might be extended (DTOs, entities). Use `type` for unions, intersections, mapped types. Prefer `interface` for public APIs (better error messages).\n00047| - Define API request/response types separately from domain models: `type CreateUserRequest = { email: string; name: string }`, `type UserResponse = { id: string; email: string; name: string; createdAt: string }`. Never expose internal models directly.\n00048| - Use branded types for domain primitives: `type UserId = string & { readonly __brand: 'UserId' }; const makeUserId = (id: string): UserId => id as UserId`. Prevents mixing email with userId.\n00049| - Use Zod for runtime validation and type inference: `const CreateUserSchema = z.object({ email: z.string().email(), name: z.string().min(1) }); type CreateUserDto = z.infer<typeof CreateUserSchema>`. Single source of truth.\n00050| - Implement discriminated unions for polymorphic APIs: `type Event = { type: 'user.created'; userId: string } | { type: 'post.published'; postId: string }`. Use in event handlers, message queues.\n00051| - Use template literal types for API routes: `type HttpMethod = 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'DELETE'; type ApiRoute = \\`/api/\\${string}\\`; type Endpoint<M extends HttpMethod> = { method: M; path: ApiRoute }`.\n00052| - Define service interfaces with dependency injection in mind: `interface UserService { createUser(dto: CreateUserDto): Promise<User>; findById(id: UserId): Promise<User | null> }`. Easy to mock, test, replace implementations.\n00053| - Use generic constraints for type-safe query builders: `function where<T, K extends keyof T>(field: K, value: T[K]): Query<T>`. Ensures field exists and value matches type.\n00054| - Use utility types extensively: `Omit<User, 'password'>` for public user type, `Partial<User>` for update DTOs, `Pick<User, 'id' | 'email'>` for minimal representations.\n00055| - Implement builder pattern for complex objects: `class QueryBuilder<T> { where(field: keyof T, value: unknown): this; orderBy(field: keyof T): this; build(): Query<T> }`. Fluent API with type safety.\n00056| - Use const type parameters (TS 5.0+) for preserving literal types: `function createRoute<const T extends string>(path: T): Route<T>`. Useful for type-safe routing.\n00057| - Define database models with ORM types: For Prisma, use generated types. For custom ORMs, define entity interfaces. Always separate database models from API DTOs for loose coupling.\n00058| \n00059| ## Safety & Security\n00060| \n00061| - Validate and sanitize all external input at API boundaries. Use Zod schemas with transforms: `z.string().trim().toLowerCase()`. Never trust client input, query params, headers.\n00062| - Implement authentication with JWT or session tokens. Store tokens in httpOnly, secure, SameSite=Strict cookies. For APIs, use Authorization header: `Bearer <token>`. Validate signature and expiration.\n00063| - Use bcrypt or argon2 for password hashing. Never store plain text passwords. Use high cost factor: `bcrypt.hash(password, 12)` or `argon2.hash(password, { timeCost: 3, memoryCost: 65536 })`.\n00064| - Implement CSRF protection for state-changing operations. Use SameSite cookies or CSRF tokens. For Express, use `csurf` middleware. For Fastify, use `@fastify/csrf-protection`.\n00065| - Configure CORS properly: Allow only trusted origins. Never use `*` with credentials. Set specific origins: `{ origin: ['https://app.example.com'], credentials: true }`. Use `cors` middleware.\n00066| - Implement rate limiting per IP and per user. Use Redis-backed rate limiters: `express-rate-limit` with Redis store, or `@fastify/rate-limit`. Apply different limits to sensitive endpoints (login, signup).\n00067| - Prevent injection attacks: Use parameterized queries for SQL (never string concatenation). Use ORM query builders (Prisma, TypeORM). Validate input against allowlist patterns.\n00068| - Sanitize output for logs and responses. Never log passwords, tokens, credit cards. Implement redaction: `logger.info({ user: redact(user, ['password', 'ssn']) })`. Use `fast-redact` library.\n00069| - Implement Content Security Policy for served HTML: `helmet` middleware sets security headers. Configure CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options.\n00070| - Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual()` for comparing secrets (tokens, signatures). Prevents timing attacks. For crypto operations, use `node:crypto` module, never custom implementations.\n00071| - Implement secure session management: Rotate session IDs after login. Expire sessions after inactivity. Store sessions in Redis with TTL. Use `express-session` or `@fastify/secure-session`.\n00072| - Validate file uploads: Check file type (magic bytes, not extension), size limits, scan for malware. Store uploads outside web root. Use signed URLs for access (S3, CloudFront).\n00073| - Audit dependencies with `pnpm audit`, `npm audit`, or Socket.dev. Enable Dependabot/Renovate. Review new dependencies for supply chain attacks. Use `socket npm install` for security analysis.\n00074| - Implement security headers: Use `helmet` middleware. Enable HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin.\n00075| \n00076| ## Serialization & Data\n00077| \n00078| - Use Zod for runtime validation of API requests and external data: `const parsed = CreateUserSchema.parse(req.body)`. Throws on validation failure with detailed errors.\n00079| - Transform Zod validation errors into user-friendly API responses: `.safeParse()` returns Result type. Map errors: `error.issues.map(i => ({ field: i.path.join('.'), message: i.message }))`.\n00080| - Serialize dates as ISO 8601 strings in JSON responses: `JSON.stringify({ createdAt: new Date().toISOString() })`. Define serializers for custom types: Use `superjson` for Date, Map, Set, BigInt, RegExp.\n00081| - Implement DTO transformers: Map database models to API responses. Exclude sensitive fields (password, internal IDs). Use class-transformer or manual mappers: `function toUserResponse(user: User): UserResponse { return { id: user.id, email: user.email } }`.\n00082| - Use Prisma for type-safe database access. Define schema in `schema.prisma`, generate types with `prisma generate`. Use relations, transactions, middleware for business logic.\n00083| - Implement database migrations: Use Prisma Migrate, TypeORM migrations, or Knex. Version migrations, test rollbacks. Never modify production schema manually.\n00084| - Handle pagination with cursor-based approach for large datasets: `{ data: T[], nextCursor: string | null, hasMore: boolean }`. Encode cursor: `Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({ id, createdAt })).toString('base64')`.\n00085| - Use JSON Schema for API documentation and validation. Generate types from schema with `json-schema-to-typescript`. Or use Zod and generate JSON Schema: `zodToJsonSchema()`.\n00086| - Implement ETags for cache validation: Hash response body, set ETag header. Check `If-None-Match`, return 304 if match. Use `etag` middleware or custom implementation.\n00087| - Use Protocol Buffers for gRPC services or binary APIs. Define `.proto` schemas, generate TypeScript types with `ts-proto`. Smaller payloads, faster serialization than JSON.\n00088| - Handle BigInt serialization: JSON.stringify doesn't support BigInt. Use custom replacer: `JSON.stringify(obj, (key, value) => typeof value === 'bigint' ? value.toString() : value)` or use `json-bigint` library.\n00089| - Implement database query result caching: Use Redis for frequently accessed data. Define TTL per entity type. Invalidate on updates: `await redis.del(\\`user:\\${userId}\\`)`.\n00090| \n00091| ## Testing\n00092| \n00093| - Use Vitest over Jest for modern projects (faster, native ESM, better TypeScript support). Configure with `vitest.config.ts`. Run with `vitest run` for CI, `vitest watch` for development.\n00094| - Write unit tests colocated with code: `userService.test.ts` next to `userService.ts`. Use descriptive test names: `it('should throw ValidationError when email is invalid', async () => {})`. Follow AAA pattern.\n00095| - Write integration tests in `tests/integration/`. # TypeScript Backend Development Guidelines\\n00002| \\n00003| ## Toolchain & Build\\n00004| \\n00005| - Always use TypeScript 5.7+ with `strict: true`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true`, and `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true` in tsconfig.json. Enable `verbatimModuleSyntax` for explicit import/export control.\\n00006| - Always run build (`pnpm build`), tests (`pnpm test`), linter (`eslint --max-warnings 0`), and type-checker (`tsc --noEmit`) before finishing tasks.\\n00007| - Use `pnpm` over `npm` for faster installs and strict dependency resolution. Run `pnpm audit` and `pnpm outdated` regularly to check for vulnerabilities.\\n00008| - Configure `moduleResolution: \\\"bundler\\\"` or `\\\"node16\\\"` for Node.js projects. Use path aliases (`@/` for `src/`) in tsconfig and build config for clean imports.\\n00009| - Use `tsx` for running TypeScript directly in development: `tsx src/index.ts`. Use `tsup` or `esbuild` for production builds (faster than tsc). Configure source maps for debugging.\\n00010| - Enable `isolatedModules: true` for compatibility with fast transpilers. Avoid const enums and namespace merging patterns.\\n00011| - Use ESLint 9+ with flat config (`eslint.config.js`). Enable `@typescript-eslint/strict-type-checked` ruleset for backend code. Use Biome as faster alternative.\\n00012| - For monorepos, use pnpm workspaces with `workspace:*` protocol. Use Turborepo for build orchestration and caching. Structure as: `apps/`, `packages/`, `services/`.\\n00013| - Pin Node.js version with `.nvmrc` or `package.json` engines field. Use LTS versions (20.x or 22.x). Use Docker for consistent environments: `FROM node:22-alpine`.\\n00014| - Configure TypeScript with `skipLibCheck: true` for faster builds, `esModuleInterop: true` for CJS compatibility, `resolveJsonModule: true` for importing JSON configs.\\n00015| \\n00016| ## Error Handling\\n00017| \\n00018| - Never throw raw strings or objects. Always throw Error instances with codes: `throw new AppError('USER_NOT_FOUND', 'User not found', { userId })`. Include error codes for client handling.\\n00019| - Use discriminated unions for Result types in business logic: `type Result<T, E = Error> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: E }`. Prefer over throwing in pure functions.\\n00020| - Implement custom error hierarchy extending Error: `class ValidationError extends Error { constructor(message: string, public readonly field: string, public readonly code: string) { super(message); this.name = 'ValidationError'; Error.captureStackTrace(this, this.constructor); } }`.\\n00021| - Define domain-specific error types: `class DatabaseError`, `class AuthenticationError`, `class RateLimitError`. Include metadata for debugging: timestamp, request ID, user context.\\n00022| - Use `cause` property for error chaining (Node 16.9+): `throw new Error('Failed to create user', { cause: originalError })`. Preserves full error context through stack.\\n00023| - Implement global error handler middleware: Catch all errors, log with context, return sanitized responses. Never expose internal errors to clients: `{ code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', message: 'An error occurred' }`.\\n00024| - For HTTP APIs, map errors to status codes consistently: 400 (validation), 401 (auth), 403 (forbidden), 404 (not found), 409 (conflict), 429 (rate limit), 500 (internal). Use custom error mapper.\\n00025| - Validate external data at API boundaries with Zod schemas. Transform Zod errors into structured responses: `{ code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR', message: string, details: { field: string, message: string }[] }`.\\n00026| - Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient failures (database deadlocks, external APIs). Use `p-retry` library with jitter: `retry(() => fetchData(), { retries: 3, factor: 2 })`.\\n00027| - Use `never` return type for assertion functions: `function assertAuthenticated(user: User | null): asserts user is User { if (!user) throw new AuthError() }`. Narrows types after assertion.\\n00028| \\n00029| ## Async & Concurrency\\n00030| \\n00031| - Always use `async/await` over raw Promises. Use `Promise.all()` for parallel execution: `const [users, posts] = await Promise.all([db.users.findMany(), db.posts.findMany()])`. Never sequential awaits for independent operations.\\n00032| - Use `Promise.allSettled()` when you need all results regardless of failures. Use `Promise.race()` for timeout patterns: `Promise.race([fetchData(), timeout(5000)])`.\\n00033| - Implement proper cancellation with AbortController for HTTP requests, database queries: `const controller = new AbortController(); fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal }); setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 5000)`.\\n00034| - Use message queues (BullMQ, Bee-Queue) for background jobs and async processing. Define typed job payloads: `type EmailJob = { type: 'email'; to: string; template: string; data: Record<string, unknown> }`. Implement job retry and dead-letter queues.\\n00035| - Organize system into subsystems using message-passing architecture. Use EventEmitter or custom event bus for internal events. For complex workflows, use state machines with XState.\\n00036| - For CPU-intensive tasks, use worker threads (`node:worker_threads`). Communicate via `postMessage()` with typed messages. Use Piscina for worker pool management. Never block event loop.\\n00037| - Avoid shared state between requests. Use request-scoped context with AsyncLocalStorage: `const requestContext = new AsyncLocalStorage<{ requestId: string; userId?: string }>()`. Access in nested functions without passing explicitly.\\n00038| - Implement graceful shutdown: Listen for SIGTERM/SIGINT, stop accepting new connections, drain active requests, close database connections, flush logs. Use `@fastify/graceful-shutdown` or custom implementation.\\n00039| - Use streaming for large payloads: Node.js streams, async iterators. Process data in chunks to avoid memory issues: `for await (const chunk of readStream) { await processChunk(chunk) }`.\\n00040| - Handle uncaught errors: `process.on('uncaughtException')`, `process.on('unhandledRejection')`. Log error, clean up resources, gracefully exit. Use process managers (PM2, Kubernetes) for restart.\\n00041| - Use connection pooling for databases (Prisma, TypeORM), Redis, HTTP clients. Configure pool size based on workload: Start with `max: 10`, tune based on monitoring.\\n00042| - Implement circuit breakers for external dependencies using `opossum`. Open circuit after threshold failures, prevent cascading failures. Use fallback responses during circuit open.\\n00043| \\n00044| ## Type Design & API\\n00045| \\n00046| - Use `interface` for object shapes that might be extended (DTOs, entities). Use `type` for unions, intersections, mapped types. Prefer `interface` for public APIs (better error messages).\\n00047| - Define API request/response types separately from domain models: `type CreateUserRequest = { email: string; name: string }`, `type UserResponse = { id: string; email: string; name: string; createdAt: string }`. Never expose internal models directly.\\n00048| - Use branded types for domain primitives: `type UserId = string & { readonly __brand: 'UserId' }; const makeUserId = (id: string): UserId => id as UserId`. Prevents mixing email with userId.\\n00049| - Use Zod for runtime validation and type inference: `const CreateUserSchema = z.object({ email: z.string().email(), name: z.string().min(1) }); type CreateUserDto = z.infer<typeof CreateUserSchema>`. Single source of truth.\\n00050| - Implement discriminated unions for polymorphic APIs: `type Event = { type: 'user.created'; userId: string } | { type: 'post.published'; postId: string }`. Use in event handlers, message queues.\\n00051| - Use template literal types for API routes: `type HttpMethod = 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'DELETE'; type ApiRoute = \\\\`/api/\\\\${string}\\\\`; type Endpoint<M extends HttpMethod> = { method: M; path: ApiRoute }`.\\n00052| - Define service interfaces with dependency injection in mind: `interface UserService { createUser(dto: CreateUserDto): Promise<User>; findById(id: UserId): Promise<User | null> }`. Easy to mock, test, replace implementations.\\n00053| - Use generic constraints for type-safe query builders: `function where<T, K extends keyof T>(field: K, value: T[K]): Query<T>`. Ensures field exists and value matches type.\\n00054| - Use utility types extensively: `Omit<User, 'password'>` for public user type, `Partial<User>` for update DTOs, `Pick<User, 'id' | 'email'>` for minimal representations.\\n00055| - Implement builder pattern for complex objects: `class QueryBuilder<T> { where(field: keyof T, value: unknown): this; orderBy(field: keyof T): this; build(): Query<T> }`. Fluent API with type safety.\\n00056| - Use const type parameters (TS 5.0+) for preserving literal types: `function createRoute<const T extends string>(path: T): Route<T>`. Useful for type-safe routing.\\n00057| - Define database models with ORM types: For Prisma, use generated types. For custom ORMs, define entity interfaces. Always separate database models from API DTOs for loose coupling.\\n00058| \\n00059| ## Safety & Security\\n00060| \\n00061| - Validate and sanitize all external input at API boundaries. Use Zod schemas with transforms: `z.string().trim().toLowerCase()`. Never trust client input, query params, headers.\\n00062| - Implement authentication with JWT or session tokens. Store tokens in httpOnly, secure, SameSite=Strict cookies. For APIs, use Authorization header: `Bearer <token>`. Validate signature and expiration.\\n00063| - Use bcrypt or argon2 for password hashing. Never store plain text passwords. Use high cost factor: `bcrypt.hash(password, 12)` or `argon2.hash(password, { timeCost: 3, memoryCost: 65536 })`.\\n00064| - Implement CSRF protection for state-changing operations. Use SameSite cookies or CSRF tokens. For Express, use `csurf` middleware. For Fastify, use `@fastify/csrf-protection`.\\n00065| - Configure CORS properly: Allow only trusted origins. Never use `*` with credentials. Set specific origins: `{ origin: ['https://app.example.com'], credentials: true }`. Use `cors` middleware.\\n00066| - Implement rate limiting per IP and per user. Use Redis-backed rate limiters: `express-rate-limit` with Redis store, or `@fastify/rate-limit`. Apply different limits to sensitive endpoints (login, signup).\\n00067| - Prevent injection attacks: Use parameterized queries for SQL (never string concatenation). Use ORM query builders (Prisma, TypeORM). Validate input against allowlist patterns.\\n00068| - Sanitize output for logs and responses. Never log passwords, tokens, credit cards. Implement redaction: `logger.info({ user: redact(user, ['password', 'ssn']) })`. Use `fast-redact` library.\\n00069| - Implement Content Security Policy for served HTML: `helmet` middleware sets security headers. Configure CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options.\\n00070| - Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual()` for comparing secrets (tokens, signatures). Prevents timing attacks. For crypto operations, use `node:crypto` module, never custom implementations.\\n00071| - Implement secure session management: Rotate session IDs after login. Expire sessions after inactivity. Store sessions in Redis with TTL. Use `express-session` or `@fastify/secure-session`.\\n00072| - Validate file uploads: Check file type (magic bytes, not extension), size limits, scan for malware. Store uploads outside web root. Use signed URLs for access (S3, CloudFront).\\n00073| - Audit dependencies with `pnpm audit`, `npm audit`, or Socket.dev. Enable Dependabot/Renovate. Review new dependencies for supply chain attacks. Use `socket npm install` for security analysis.\\n00074| - Implement security headers: Use `helmet` middleware. Enable HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin.\\n00075| \\n00076| ## Serialization & Data\\n00077| \\n00078| - Use Zod for runtime validation of API requests and external data: `const parsed = CreateUserSchema.parse(req.body)`. Throws on validation failure with detailed errors.\\n00079| - Transform Zod validation errors into user-friendly API responses: `.safeParse()` returns Result type. Map errors: `error.issues.map(i => ({ field: i.path.join('.'), message: i.message }))`.\\n00080| - Serialize dates as ISO 8601 strings in JSON responses: `JSON.stringify({ createdAt: new Date().toISOString() })`. Define serializers for custom types: Use `superjson` for Date, Map, Set, BigInt, RegExp.\\n00081| - Implement DTO transformers: Map database models to API responses. Exclude sensitive fields (password, internal IDs). Use class-transformer or manual mappers: `function toUserResponse(user: User): UserResponse { return { id: user.id, email: user.email } }`.\\n00082| - Use Prisma for type-safe database access. Define schema in `schema.prisma`, generate types with `prisma generate`. Use relations, transactions, middleware for business logic.\\n00083| - Implement database migrations: Use Prisma Migrate, TypeORM migrations, or Knex. Version migrations, test rollbacks. Never modify production schema manually.\\n00084| - Handle pagination with cursor-based approach for large datasets: `{ data: T[], nextCursor: string | null, hasMore: boolean }`. Invalidate on updates: `await redis.del(\\\\`user:\\\\${userId}\\\\`)`.\\n00090| \\n00091| ## Testing\\n00092| \\n00093| - Use Vitest over Jest for modern projects (faster, native ESM, better TypeScript support). Track business metrics (signups, orders, revenue) alongside technical metrics. Create dashboards for observability.\\n00120| \\n00121| ## Performance\\n00122| \\n00123| - Profile before optimizing: Use Node.js built-in profiler (`node --prof`), Chrome DevTools (inspect mode), or `clinic.js` for flame graphs, heap analysis, event loop analysis.\\n00124| - Optimize database queries: Use indexes on frequently queried fields. Avoid N+1 queries (use joins or dataloader). Use `EXPLAIN` to analyze query plans. Add pagination to large result sets.\\n00125| - Implement caching strategy: Cache frequently accessed data in Redis with TTL. Use cache-aside pattern: Check cache, miss → fetch from DB → set cache. Define cache key convention: `entity:id`.\\n00126| - Use connection pooling: Configure database pool size based on workload. For Prisma: `connection_limit` in database URL. For Redis: `ioredis` with pool. Monitor pool exhaustion.\\n00127| - Optimize JSON serialization: Use `fast-json-stringify` with JSON Schema for 2-3x faster serialization. For large responses, use streaming: `res.write()` chunks instead of single `res.json()`.\\n00128| - Implement response compression: Use `compression` middleware (gzip, brotli). Configure level vs speed tradeoff. Enable for text responses (JSON, HTML), skip for images, video.\\n00129| - Use clustering for CPU utilization: Node.js is single-threaded. Use `cluster` module to spawn workers per CPU core. Or deploy multiple instances behind load balancer (better for containers).\\n00130| - Optimize cold starts: Minimize startup work. Lazy load heavy dependencies. Use `import()` for conditional imports. For serverless (AWS Lambda), reduce bundle size, use provisioned concurrency.\\n00131| - Implement request coalescing: Deduplicate concurrent identical requests (e.g., same user requesting same resource multiple times). Use in-memory Map to track pending requests.\\n00132| - Use async iterators for streaming large datasets: `async function* fetchUsers() { for (const batch of batches) { yield* batch } }`. Process in chunks to avoid loading entire dataset in memory.\\n00133| - Monitor event loop lag: Use `toobusy-js` or custom monitoring: `const start = Date.now(); setImmediate(() => { const lag = Date.now() - start })`. Alert when lag exceeds threshold (indicates blocked event loop).\\n00134| - Optimize Docker images: Use multi-stage builds. Use alpine base image. Copy only production dependencies: `pnpm install --prod`. Remove dev dependencies and cache. Use `.dockerignore`.\\n00135| \\n00136| ## Dependencies\\n00137| \\n00138| - Minimize dependencies: Each adds bundle size, security risk, maintenance burden. Evaluate necessity before adding. Implement simple utilities instead of adding library (e.g., retry logic vs full library).\\n00139| - Audit dependencies before adding: Check npm downloads, GitHub stars, last update date, open issues, security advisories. Use `npx socket npm install <package>` for security analysis. Avoid packages with install scripts.\\n00140| - Pin exact versions in package.json for applications: Use `\\\"fastify\\\": \\\"5.2.0\\\"` not `\\\"^5.2.0\\\"`. Use `p-retry` library with jitter: `retry(() => fetchData(), { retries: 3, factor: 2 })`.\n- Use `never` return type for assertion functions: `function assertAuthenticated(user: User | null): asserts user is User { if (!user) throw new AuthError() }`. Narrows types after assertion.\n\n## Async & Concurrency\n\n- Always use `async/await` over raw Promises. Use `Promise.all()` for parallel execution: `const [users, posts] = await Promise.all([db.users.findMany(), db.posts.findMany()])`. Never sequential awaits for independent operations.\n- Use `Promise.allSettled()` when you need all results regardless of failures. Use `Promise.race()` for timeout patterns: `Promise.race([fetchData(), timeout(5000)])`.\n- Implement proper cancellation with AbortController for HTTP requests, database queries: `const controller = new AbortController(); fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal }); setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 5000)`.\n- Use message queues (BullMQ, Bee-Queue) for background jobs and async processing. Define typed job payloads: `type EmailJob = { type: 'email'; to: string; template: string; data: Record<string, unknown> }`. Implement job retry and dead-letter queues.\n- Organize system into subsystems using message-passing architecture. Use EventEmitter or custom event bus for internal events. For complex workflows, use state machines with XState.\n- For CPU-intensive tasks, use worker threads (`node:worker_threads`). Communicate via `postMessage()` with typed messages. Use Piscina for worker pool management. Never block event loop.\n- Avoid shared state between requests. Use request-scoped context with AsyncLocalStorage: `const requestContext = new AsyncLocalStorage<{ requestId: string; userId?: string }>()`. Access in nested functions without passing explicitly.\n- Implement graceful shutdown: Listen for SIGTERM/SIGINT, stop accepting new connections, drain active requests, close database connections, flush logs. Use `@fastify/graceful-shutdown` or custom implementation.\n- Use streaming for large payloads: Node.js streams, async iterators. Process data in chunks to avoid memory issues: `for await (const chunk of readStream) { await processChunk(chunk) }`.\n- Handle uncaught errors: `process.on('uncaughtException')`, `process.on('unhandledRejection')`. Log error, clean up resources, gracefully exit. Use process managers (PM2, Kubernetes) for restart.\n- Use connection pooling for databases (Prisma, TypeORM), Redis, HTTP clients. Configure pool size based on workload: Start with `max: 10`, tune based on monitoring.\n- Implement circuit breakers for external dependencies using `opossum`. Open circuit after threshold failures, prevent cascading failures. Use fallback responses during circuit open.\n\n## Type Design & API\n\n- Use `interface` for object shapes that might be extended (DTOs, entities). Use `type` for unions, intersections, mapped types. Prefer `interface` for public APIs (better error messages).\n- Define API request/response types separately from domain models: `type CreateUserRequest = { email: string; name: string }`, `type UserResponse = { id: string; email: string; name: string; createdAt: string }`. Never expose internal models directly.\n- Use branded types for domain primitives: `type UserId = string & { readonly __brand: 'UserId' }; const makeUserId = (id: string): UserId => id as UserId`. Prevents mixing email with userId.\n- Use Zod for runtime validation and type inference: `const CreateUserSchema = z.object({ email: z.string().email(), name: z.string().min(1) }); type CreateUserDto = z.infer<typeof CreateUserSchema>`. Single source of truth.\n- Implement discriminated unions for polymorphic APIs: `type Event = { type: 'user.created'; userId: string } | { type: 'post.published'; postId: string }`. Use in event handlers, message queues.\n- Use template literal types for API routes: `type HttpMethod = 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'DELETE'; type ApiRoute = \\`/api/\\${string}\\`; type Endpoint<M extends HttpMethod> = { method: M; path: ApiRoute }`.\n- Define service interfaces with dependency injection in mind: `interface UserService { createUser(dto: CreateUserDto): Promise<User>; findById(id: UserId): Promise<User | null> }`. Easy to mock, test, replace implementations.\n- Use generic constraints for type-safe query builders: `function where<T, K extends keyof T>(field: K, value: T[K]): Query<T>`. Ensures field exists and value matches type.\n- Use utility types extensively: `Omit<User, 'password'>` for public user type, `Partial<User>` for update DTOs, `Pick<User, 'id' | 'email'>` for minimal representations.\n- Implement builder pattern for complex objects: `class QueryBuilder<T> { where(field: keyof T, value: unknown): this; orderBy(field: keyof T): this; build(): Query<T> }`. Fluent API with type safety.\n- Use const type parameters (TS 5.0+) for preserving literal types: `function createRoute<const T extends string>(path: T): Route<T>`. Useful for type-safe routing.\n- Define database models with ORM types: For Prisma, use generated types. For custom ORMs, define entity interfaces. Always separate database models from API DTOs for loose coupling.\n\n## Safety & Security\n\n- Validate and sanitize all external input at API boundaries. Use Zod schemas with transforms: `z.string().trim().toLowerCase()`. Never trust client input, query params, headers.\n- Implement authentication with JWT or session tokens. Store tokens in httpOnly, secure, SameSite=Strict cookies. For APIs, use Authorization header: `Bearer <token>`. Validate signature and expiration.\n- Use bcrypt or argon2 for password hashing. Never store plain text passwords. Use high cost factor: `bcrypt.hash(password, 12)` or `argon2.hash(password, { timeCost: 3, memoryCost: 65536 })`.\n- Implement CSRF protection for state-changing operations. Use SameSite cookies or CSRF tokens. For Express, use `csurf` middleware. For Fastify, use `@fastify/csrf-protection`.\n- Configure CORS properly: Allow only trusted origins. Never use `*` with credentials. Set specific origins: `{ origin: ['https://app.example.com'], credentials: true }`. Use `cors` middleware.\n- Implement rate limiting per IP and per user. Use Redis-backed rate limiters: `express-rate-limit` with Redis store, or `@fastify/rate-limit`. Apply different limits to sensitive endpoints (login, signup).\n- Prevent injection attacks: Use parameterized queries for SQL (never string concatenation). Use ORM query builders (Prisma, TypeORM). Validate input against allowlist patterns.\n- Sanitize output for logs and responses. Never log passwords, tokens, credit cards. Implement redaction: `logger.info({ user: redact(user, ['password', 'ssn']) })`. Use `fast-redact` library.\n- Implement Content Security Policy for served HTML: `helmet` middleware sets security headers. Configure CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options.\n- Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual()` for comparing secrets (tokens, signatures). Prevents timing attacks. For crypto operations, use `node:crypto` module, never custom implementations.\n- Implement secure session management: Rotate session IDs after login. Expire sessions after inactivity. Store sessions in Redis with TTL. Use `express-session` or `@fastify/secure-session`.\n- Validate file uploads: Check file type (magic bytes, not extension), size limits, scan for malware. Store uploads outside web root. Use signed URLs for access (S3, CloudFront).\n- Audit dependencies with `pnpm audit`, `npm audit`, or Socket.dev. Enable Dependabot/Renovate. Review new dependencies for supply chain attacks. Use `socket npm install` for security analysis.\n- Implement security headers: Use `helmet` middleware. Enable HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin.\n\n## Serialization & Data\n\n- Use Zod for runtime validation of API requests and external data: `const parsed = CreateUserSchema.parse(req.body)`. Throws on validation failure with detailed errors.\n- Transform Zod validation errors into user-friendly API responses: `.safeParse()` returns Result type. Map errors: `error.issues.map(i => ({ field: i.path.join('.'), message: i.message }))`.\n- Serialize dates as ISO 8601 strings in JSON responses: `JSON.stringify({ createdAt: new Date().toISOString() })`. Define serializers for custom types: Use `superjson` for Date, Map, Set, BigInt, RegExp.\n- Implement DTO transformers: Map database models to API responses. Exclude sensitive fields (password, internal IDs). Use class-transformer or manual mappers: `function toUserResponse(user: User): UserResponse { return { id: user.id, email: user.email } }`.\n- Use Prisma for type-safe database access. Define schema in `schema.prisma`, generate types with `prisma generate`. Use relations, transactions, middleware for business logic.\n- Implement database migrations: Use Prisma Migrate, TypeORM migrations, or Knex. Version migrations, test rollbacks. Never modify production schema manually.\n- Handle pagination with cursor-based approach for large datasets: `{ data: T[], nextCursor: string | null, hasMore: boolean }`. Encode cursor: `Buffer.from(JSON.stringify({ id, createdAt })).toString('base64')`.\n- Use JSON Schema for API documentation and validation. Generate types from schema with `json-schema-to-typescript`. Or use Zod and generate JSON Schema: `zodToJsonSchema()`.\n- Implement ETags for cache validation: Hash response body, set ETag header. Check `If-None-Match`, return 304 if match. Use `etag` middleware or custom implementation.\n- Use Protocol Buffers for gRPC services or binary APIs. Define `.proto` schemas, generate TypeScript types with `ts-proto`. Smaller payloads, faster serialization than JSON.\n- Handle BigInt serialization: JSON.stringify doesn't support BigInt. Use custom replacer: `JSON.stringify(obj, (key, value) => typeof value === 'bigint' ? value.toString() : value)` or use `json-bigint` library.\n- Implement database query result caching: Use Redis for frequently accessed data. Define TTL per entity type. Invalidate on updates: `await redis.del(\\`user:\\${userId}\\`)`.\n\n## Testing\n\n- Use Vitest over Jest for modern projects (faster, native ESM, better TypeScript support). Configure with `vitest.config.ts`. Run with `vitest run` for CI, `vitest watch` for development.\n- Write unit tests colocated with code: `userService.test.ts` next to `userService.ts`. Use descriptive test names: `it('should throw ValidationError when email is invalid', async () => {})`. Follow AAA pattern.\n- Write integration tests in `tests/integration/`. Test API endpoints end-to-end with real database (use test database). Use supertest or native fetch: `const response = await fetch('http://localhost:3000/api/users', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(data) })`.\n- Use test fixtures for database data: Create factory functions: `function createUser(overrides?: Partial<User>): Promise<User>`. Use `@faker-js/faker` for generating realistic test data.\n- Mock external dependencies (third-party APIs, email services) with MSW (Mock Service Worker) for HTTP or `vi.mock()` for modules. Test error scenarios: network failures, timeouts, rate limits.\n- Test database interactions with test containers (Testcontainers) or in-memory databases (better-sqlite3). Isolate tests: Clear database between tests or use transactions: `beforeEach(async () => { await db.truncate() })`.\n- Test authentication and authorization: Mock auth tokens, test protected endpoints return 401/403. Test role-based access: `it('should return 403 when user lacks admin role', async () => {})`.\n- Test error handling explicitly: Verify error codes, status codes, error messages. Use `expect().rejects.toThrow()` for async errors. Test validation errors return proper structure.\n- Use snapshot tests sparingly (only for complex responses). Prefer explicit assertions: `expect(response.status).toBe(200); expect(response.body).toMatchObject({ id: expect.any(String), email: 'test@example.com' })`.\n- Implement E2E tests with Playwright for critical user flows. Test across different databases, environments. Run in CI with Docker Compose: database, Redis, app.\n- Aim for 80%+ coverage on business logic. Use `v8` coverage in Vitest: `vitest --coverage`. Generate reports: `--reporter=html`. Focus on critical paths: auth, payments, data mutations.\n- Test concurrency issues: Race conditions, deadlocks. Use Promise.all to trigger parallel operations: `await Promise.all([updateUser(1), updateUser(1)])`. Verify proper locking or optimistic locking.\n\n## Logging & Observability\n\n- Use Pino for structured logging (fastest JSON logger for Node.js). Configure with `pino({ level: process.env.LOG_LEVEL || 'info', formatters: { level: (label) => ({ level: label }) } })`. Use pretty printing in dev: `pino-pretty`.\n- Implement different log levels: `fatal` for crashes, `error` for errors requiring attention, `warn` for degraded state, `info` for important events (API calls, user actions), `debug` and `trace` for diagnostics.\n- Add request context to all logs: request ID, user ID, session ID. Use AsyncLocalStorage to propagate context: `const storage = new AsyncLocalStorage<Context>()`. Create middleware to inject context: `req.log = logger.child({ requestId: uuid(), userId: req.user?.id })`.\n- Log structured data with fields: `logger.info({ userId, action: 'user.created', duration: 123 }, 'User created successfully')`. Enables querying logs by fields. Never concatenate strings: `logger.info('User ' + id)`.\n- Integrate error tracking with Sentry, Bugsnag, or Rollbar. Initialize with DSN: `Sentry.init({ dsn: process.env.SENTRY_DSN, environment: process.env.NODE_ENV })`. Capture errors: `Sentry.captureException(error)`. Set context: `Sentry.setUser()`, `Sentry.setTag()`.\n- Implement distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry. Instrument with auto-instrumentation: `@opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node`. Export traces to Jaeger, Zipkin, Datadog, New Relic. Add custom spans for business logic.\n- Log all API requests/responses in development. Redact sensitive data (tokens, passwords, SSN) in production logs. Use `fast-redact` or custom redaction: `logger.child({ redact: ['password', 'token'] })`.\n- Monitor application metrics: Request rate, error rate, latency (p50, p95, p99), active connections. Use Prometheus with `prom-client`: `const httpRequestDuration = new Histogram({ name: 'http_request_duration_seconds', help: 'Duration of HTTP requests in seconds' })`.\n- Implement health checks: `/health` endpoint returning 200 when healthy. Check database connectivity, Redis, external dependencies. Use for load balancer health checks, Kubernetes liveness/readiness probes.\n- Set up alerting: Error rate spikes, high latency, failed health checks. Use PagerDuty, Opsgenie, or cloud provider alerts. Define SLOs and alert on SLO violations.\n- Use structured logs for audit trail: Log all state-changing operations (create, update, delete) with actor, timestamp, old/new values. Store in separate audit log table or log aggregation service.\n- Collect and analyze metrics: Use Datadog, New Relic, Prometheus + Grafana. Track business metrics (signups, orders, revenue) alongside technical metrics. Create dashboards for observability.\n\n## Performance\n\n- Profile before optimizing: Use Node.js built-in profiler (`node --prof`), Chrome DevTools (inspect mode), or `clinic.js` for flame graphs, heap analysis, event loop analysis.\n- Optimize database queries: Use indexes on frequently queried fields. Avoid N+1 queries (use joins or dataloader). Use `EXPLAIN` to analyze query plans. Add pagination to large result sets.\n- Implement caching strategy: Cache frequently accessed data in Redis with TTL. Use cache-aside pattern: Check cache, miss → fetch from DB → set cache. Define cache key convention: `entity:id`.\n- Use connection pooling: Configure database pool size based on workload. For Prisma: `connection_limit` in database URL. For Redis: `ioredis` with pool. Monitor pool exhaustion.\n- Optimize JSON serialization: Use `fast-json-stringify` with JSON Schema for 2-3x faster serialization. For large responses, use streaming: `res.write()` chunks instead of single `res.json()`.\n- Implement response compression: Use `compression` middleware (gzip, brotli). Configure level vs speed tradeoff. Enable for text responses (JSON, HTML), skip for images, video.\n- Use clustering for CPU utilization: Node.js is single-threaded. Use `cluster` module to spawn workers per CPU core. Or deploy multiple instances behind load balancer (better for containers).\n- Optimize cold starts: Minimize startup work. Lazy load heavy dependencies. Use `import()` for conditional imports. For serverless (AWS Lambda), reduce bundle size, use provisioned concurrency.\n- Implement request coalescing: Deduplicate concurrent identical requests (e.g., same user requesting same resource multiple times). Use in-memory Map to track pending requests.\n- Use async iterators for streaming large datasets: `async function* fetchUsers() { for (const batch of batches) { yield* batch } }`. Process in chunks to avoid loading entire dataset in memory.\n- Monitor event loop lag: Use `toobusy-js` or custom monitoring: `const start = Date.now(); setImmediate(() => { const lag = Date.now() - start })`. Alert when lag exceeds threshold (indicates blocked event loop).\n- Optimize Docker images: Use multi-stage builds. Use alpine base image. Copy only production dependencies: `pnpm install --prod`. Remove dev dependencies and cache. Use `.dockerignore`.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- Minimize dependencies: Each adds bundle size, security risk, maintenance burden. Evaluate necessity before adding. Implement simple utilities instead of adding library (e.g., retry logic vs full library).\n- Audit dependencies before adding: Check npm downloads, GitHub stars, last update date, open issues, security advisories. Use `npx socket npm install <package>` for security analysis. Avoid packages with install scripts.\n- Pin exact versions in package.json for applications: Use `\"fastify\": \"5.2.0\"` not `\"^5.2.0\"`. Prevents unexpected breakages in production. Use Renovate or Dependabot for automated updates with testing.\n- Prefer well-maintained, popular packages with TypeScript support. Check for `@types/*` packages or built-in types. Avoid packages requiring manual type definitions.\n- Use workspace dependencies in monorepos: Define in `[workspace.dependencies]` in root package.json. Use `workspace:*` for internal packages. Ensures consistent versions across services.\n- Avoid mixing ESM and CJS dependencies when possible. Prefer pure ESM packages for modern Node.js. Check `package.json` for `\"type\": \"module\"` and `\"exports\"` field.\n- Replace heavy dependencies with lighter alternatives: Use `pino` over `winston`, `ky` over `axios`, `postgres` over `pg` + `pg-promise`. Check bundle size impact.\n- Keep dependencies updated: Run `pnpm update` monthly. Review changelogs before major updates. Test thoroughly. Use `npm-check-updates` for bulk updates: `npx ncu -u`.\n- Remove unused dependencies: Run `depcheck` to find unused deps. Remove `devDependencies` not used in scripts. Check for duplicate packages: `pnpm list --depth=Infinity | grep <package>`.\n- Lock dependency versions with `pnpm-lock.yaml`. Commit to git. Use `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in CI/production to ensure reproducible builds. Never use `npm update` without testing.\n\n## Documentation\n\n- Write TSDoc comments for exported functions, classes, types: `/** Creates a new user. @param dto - User creation data. @returns Created user with generated ID. @throws {ValidationError} When email is invalid. @example \\`\\`\\`ts\\nawait createUser({ email: 'user@example.com', name: 'John' })\\n\\`\\`\\` */`.\n- Document API endpoints with OpenAPI/Swagger: Use `@fastify/swagger` or `swagger-jsdoc`. Generate interactive docs. Define request/response schemas with Zod or JSON Schema. Host on `/docs` endpoint.\n- Document environment variables in `.env.example` with comments: `# Database connection string (required)\\nDATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/db`. Use `dotenv` for loading, `envalid` for validation.\n- Generate API client types from OpenAPI spec using `openapi-typescript` or Zod schemas. Share types between backend and frontend. Version APIs with `/v1/`, `/v2/` prefixes.\n- Write README.md for services/packages: Include installation, configuration, API endpoints, authentication, error codes, examples. Document deployment process, environment requirements.\n- Document architecture decisions with ADRs (Architecture Decision Records) in `docs/adr/`. Use template: Title, Status, Context, Decision, Consequences. Number sequentially: `001-use-postgresql-over-mongodb.md`.\n- Add inline comments for complex business logic only. Code should be self-documenting with clear names. Comment \"why\" not \"what\": `// Use pessimistic locking to prevent race condition in payment processing` not `// Lock row`.\n- Document error codes in centralized location: Create enum or object mapping codes to descriptions. Include in API documentation. Example: `USER_NOT_FOUND: 'User with specified ID does not exist'`.\n- Create runbooks for operational procedures: Deployment, rollback, database migrations, scaling, incident response. Store in `docs/runbooks/`. Include commands, expected outputs, troubleshooting steps.\n- Document database schema: Generate ER diagrams from Prisma schema. Document table purposes, indexes, constraints. Explain complex queries or stored procedures. Use `prisma-docs` or `dbdocs.io`.\n\n## Code Style\n\n- Use functional programming principles: Pure functions, immutability, composition. Avoid mutations: Use `map/filter/reduce` over `for` loops modifying arrays. Use spread operator: `{ ...obj, key: newValue }`.\n- Follow naming conventions: `camelCase` for variables/functions, `PascalCase` for types/interfaces/classes, `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` for constants. Use descriptive names: `fetchUserById` not `getUser`.\n- Keep functions small and focused: <50 lines ideally. Single responsibility. Extract complex logic into well-named helper functions. Use early returns: `if (!user) return null;`.\n- Order imports consistently: Node.js built-ins first (`node:fs`, `node:path`), external dependencies second (alphabetically), internal modules third (`@/services/*`), types fourth. Use auto-sorting with `eslint-plugin-import`.\n- Use const by default, let only when reassignment needed. Never use var. Use destructuring: `const { id, email } = user` not `const id = user.id`.\n- Prefer arrow functions for callbacks and inline functions: `const double = (x: number) => x * 2`. Use function declarations for top-level exported functions, methods.\n- Use template literals for string interpolation: `` `User ${id} not found` `` not `'User ' + id + ' not found'`. Use template literals for multi-line strings, SQL queries.\n- Avoid nested ternaries. Use if/else or extract to functions. Max one ternary per line: `const status = isActive ? 'active' : 'inactive'`. For multiple conditions, use switch or object lookup.\n- Use optional chaining: `user?.profile?.avatar` instead of `user && user.profile && user.profile.avatar`. Use nullish coalescing: `value ?? defaultValue` (handles `0`, `''`, `false` correctly).\n- Export functions as named exports: `export async function createUser(dto: CreateUserDto): Promise<User>`. Better for tree-shaking, refactoring. Use default exports sparingly (e.g., Express app).\n- Use trailing commas in multi-line arrays, objects, function parameters: Cleaner git diffs, easier to reorder lines. Prettier enforces this with `trailingComma: 'all'`.\n- Organize files consistently: Imports → Constants → Types → Functions → Exports. Group related functions. Use barrel exports (`index.ts`) for clean imports: `import { createUser, findUser } from '@/services/user'`.\n- Use async/await consistently. Never mix promises and callbacks. Handle errors with try/catch at boundaries. Use `.catch()` only when truly recovering from error, not for logging.\n- Prefer composition over inheritance. Use dependency injection for testability. Define interfaces for services, implement with classes or functions.
