ending in TypeScript extensions to their corresponding JavaScript extensions. Non-relative paths and paths without extensions are unaffected.\n\n```typescript\n// Under --rewriteRelativeImportExtensions...\n// these will be rewritten.\nimport * as foo from \"./foo.ts\";\nimport * as bar from \"../someFolder/bar.mts\";\n// these will NOT be rewritten in any way.\nimport * as a from \"./foo\";\nimport * as b from \"some-package/file.ts\";\nimport * as c from \"@some-scope/some-package/file.ts\";\nimport * as d from \"#/file.ts\";\nimport * as e from \"./file.js\";\n\n```\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Importing TypeScript Files with AllowImportingTsExtensions Enabled\n\nSource: https://github.com/context7/typescriptlang/blob/main/handbook/modules/theory.md\n\nThis TypeScript code example demonstrates importing a module using its '.ts' extension. This is permissible when the 'allowImportingTsExtensions' compiler option is enabled, preventing a compile-time error related to using TypeScript file extensions in import paths. The example shows a potential error message if this option were not enabled.\n\n```typescript\n// @Filename: src/math.ts\nexport function add(a: number, b: number) {\n  return a + b;\n}\n// @Filename: src/main.ts\nimport { add } from \"./math.ts\";\n//                  ^^^^^^^^^^^\n// An import path can only end with a '.ts' extension when 'allowImportingTsExtensions' is enabled.\n\n```\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### TypeScript 5.7: ES2024 Target and Lib Support\n\nSource: https://github.com/context7/typescriptlang/blob/main/handbook/release-notes/typescript-5-7.md\n\nDefines a generic interface for Uint8Array, allowing it to work with different ArrayBuffer types. This change is part of the ES2024 target support, providing more flexibility with SharedArrayBuffer and ArrayBuffer operations.\n\n```typescript\ninterface Uint8Array<TArrayBuffer extends ArrayBufferLike = ArrayBufferLike> {\n    // ...\n}\n```\n\n### Path Rewriting for Relative Paths\n\nSource: https://github.com/context7/typescriptlang/blob/main/handbook/release-notes/typescript-5-7.md\n\nThe `--rewriteRelativeImportExtensions` compiler option addresses the need to generate JavaScript files from TypeScript source while maintaining compatibility with in-place execution. When this option is enabled, the TypeScript compiler rewrites relative import paths (those starting with `./` or `../`) that end with a TypeScript extension (`.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mts`, `.cts`) and are not declaration files. The paths are rewritten to their corresponding JavaScript extensions (`.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`). This allows developers to write code that can be run directly using TypeScript extensions and then compiled into standard JavaScript files for distribution.\n\n--------------------------------\n\n### Path Rewriting for Relative Paths\n\nSource: https://github.com/context7/typescriptlang/blob/main/handbook/release-notes/typescript-5-7.md\n\nTypeScript historically avoided rewriting paths for several reasons, including the complexity of handling dynamic imports and the naive rewriting of only relative paths. Dynamic imports, where the import path is determined at runtime, make it impossible for the compiler to reliably rewrite the path. Additionally, paths that rely on TypeScript's `baseUrl` and `paths` compiler options, or those resolved through the `exports` and `imports` fields in `package.json`, are not rewritten by `--rewriteRelativeImportExtensions`. Invalidate on updates: `await redis.del(\\`user:\\${userId}\\`)`.\n\n## Testing\n\n- Use Vitest over Jest for modern projects (faster, native ESM, better TypeScript support). Test API endpoints end-to-end with real database (use test database). Use AsyncLocalStorage to propagate context: `const storage = new AsyncLocalStorage<Context>()`. Create middleware to inject context: `req.log = logger.child({ requestId: uuid(), userId: req.user?.id })`.\n- Log structured data with fields: `logger.info({ userId, action: 'user.created', duration: 123 }, 'User created successfully')`. Enable `verbatimModuleSyntax` for explicit import/export control.\n00006| - Always run build (`pnpm build`), tests (`pnpm test`), linter (`eslint --max-warnings 0`), and type-checker (`tsc --noEmit`) before finishing tasks.\n00007| - Use `pnpm` over `npm` for faster installs and strict dependency resolution. Run `pnpm audit` and `pnpm outdated` regularly to check for vulnerabilities.\n00008| - Configure `moduleResolution: \"bundler\"` or `\"node16\"` for Node.js projects. Use path aliases (`@/` for `src/`) in tsconfig and build config for clean imports.\n00009| - Use `tsx` for running TypeScript directly in development: `tsx src/index.ts`. Use `tsup` or `esbuild` for production builds (faster than tsc). Configure source maps for debugging.\n00010| - Enable `isolatedModules: true` for compatibility with fast transpilers. Avoid const enums and namespace merging patterns.\n00011| - Use ESLint 9+ with flat config (`eslint.config.js`). Enable `@typescript-eslint/strict-type-checked` ruleset for backend code. Use Biome as faster alternative.\n00012| - For monorepos, use pnpm workspaces with `workspace:*` protocol. Use Turborepo for build orchestration and caching. Structure as: `apps/`, `packages/`, `services/`.\n00013| - Pin Node.js version with `.nvmrc` or `package.json` engines field. Use LTS versions (20.x or 22.x). Use Docker for consistent environments: `FROM node:22-alpine`.\n00014| - Configure TypeScript with `skipLibCheck: true` for faster builds, `esModuleInterop: true` for CJS compatibility, `resolveJsonModule: true` for importing JSON configs.\n00015| \n00016| ## Error Handling\n00017| \n00018| - Never throw raw strings or objects. Always throw Error instances with codes: `throw new AppError('USER_NOT_FOUND', 'User not found', { userId })`. Include error codes for client handling.\n00019| - Use discriminated unions for Result types in business logic: `type Result<T, E = Error> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: E }`. Prefer over throwing in pure functions.\n00020| - Implement custom error hierarchy extending Error: `class ValidationError extends Error { constructor(message: string, public readonly field: string, public readonly code: string) { super(message); this.name = 'ValidationError'; Error.captureStackTrace(this, this.constructor); } }`.\n00021| - Define domain-specific error types: `class DatabaseError`, `class AuthenticationError`, `class RateLimitError`. Include metadata for debugging: timestamp, request ID, user context.\n00022| - Use `cause` property for error chaining (Node 16.9+): `throw new Error('Failed to create user', { cause: originalError })`. Preserves full error context through stack.\n00023| - Implement global error handler middleware: Catch all errors, log with context, return sanitized responses. Never expose internal errors to clients: `{ code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', message: 'An error occurred' }`.\n00024| - For HTTP APIs, map errors to status codes consistently: 400 (validation), 401 (auth), 403 (forbidden), 404 (not found), 409 (conflict), 429 (rate limit), 500 (internal). Use custom error mapper.\n00025| - Validate external data at API boundaries with Zod schemas. Transform Zod errors into structured responses: `{ code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR', message: string, details: { field: string, message: string }[] }`.\n00026| - Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient failures (database deadlocks, external APIs). Use `p-retry` library with jitter: `retry(() => fetchData(), { retries: 3, factor: 2 })`.\n00027| - Use `never` return type for assertion functions: `function assertAuthenticated(user: User | null): asserts user is User { if (!user) throw new AuthError() }`. Narrows types after assertion.\n00028| \n00029| ## Async & Concurrency\n00030| \n00031| - Always use `async/await` over raw Promises. Use `Promise.all()` for parallel execution: `const [users, posts] = await Promise.all([db.users.findMany(), db.posts.findMany()])`. Never sequential awaits for independent operations.\n00032| - Use `Promise.allSettled()` when you need all results regardless of failures. Use `Promise.race()` for timeout patterns: `Promise.race([fetchData(), timeout(5000)])`.\n00033| - Implement proper cancellation with AbortController for HTTP requests, database queries: `const controller = new AbortController(); fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal }); setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 5000)`.\n00034| - Use message queues (BullMQ, Bee-Queue) for background jobs and async processing. Define typed job payloads: `type EmailJob = { type: 'email'; to: string; template: string; data: Record<string, unknown> }`. Implement job retry and dead-letter queues.\n00035| - Organize system into subsystems using message-passing architecture. Use EventEmitter or custom event bus for internal events. For complex workflows, use state machines with XState.\n00036| - For CPU-intensive tasks, use worker threads (`node:worker_threads`). Communicate via `postMessage()` with typed messages. Use Piscina for worker pool management. Never block event loop.\n00037| - Avoid shared state between requests. Use request-scoped context with AsyncLocalStorage: `const requestContext = new AsyncLocalStorage<{ requestId: string; userId?: string }>()`. Access in nested functions without passing explicitly.\n00038| - Implement graceful shutdown: Listen for SIGTERM/SIGINT, stop accepting new connections, drain active requests, close database connections, flush logs. Use `@fastify/graceful-shutdown` or custom implementation.\n00039| - Use streaming for large payloads: Node.js streams, async iterators. Process data in chunks to avoid memory issues: `for await (const chunk of readStream) { await processChunk(chunk) }`.\n00040| - Handle uncaught errors: `process.on('uncaughtException')`, `process.on('unhandledRejection')`. Configure pool size based on workload: Start with `max: 10`, tune based on monitoring.\n00042| - Implement circuit breakers for external dependencies using `opossum`. Open circuit after threshold failures, prevent cascading failures. Use fallback responses during circuit open.\n00043| \n00044| ## Type Design & API\n00045| \n00046| - Use `interface` for object shapes that might be extended (DTOs, entities). Use `type` for unions, intersections, mapped types. Prefer `interface` for public APIs (better error messages).\n00047| - Define API request/response types separately from domain models: `type CreateUserRequest = { email: string; name: string }`, `type UserResponse = { id: string; email: string; name: string; createdAt: string }`. Ensures field exists and value matches type.\n00054| - Use utility types extensively: `Omit<User, 'password'>` for public user type, `Partial<User>` for update DTOs, `Pick<User, 'id' | 'email'>` for minimal representations.\n00055| - Implement builder pattern for complex objects: `class QueryBuilder<T> { where(field: keyof T, value: unknown): this; orderBy(field: keyof T): this; build(): Query<T> }`. Fluent API with type safety.\n00056| - Use const type parameters (TS 5.0+) for preserving literal types: `function createRoute<const T extends string>(path: T): Route<T>`. Useful for type-safe routing.\n00057| - Define database models with ORM types: For Prisma, use generated types. For custom ORMs, define entity interfaces. Always separate database models from API DTOs for loose coupling.\n00058| \n00059| ## Safety & Security\n00060| \n00061| - Validate and sanitize all external input at API boundaries. Use Zod schemas with transforms: `z.string().trim().toLowerCase()`. Never trust client input, query params, headers.\n00062| - Implement authentication with JWT or session tokens. Store tokens in httpOnly, secure, SameSite=Strict cookies. For APIs, use Authorization header: `Bearer <token>`. Validate signature and expiration.\n00063| - Use bcrypt or argon2 for password hashing. Never store plain text passwords. Use high cost factor: `bcrypt.hash(password, 12)` or `argon2.hash(password, { timeCost: 3, memoryCost: 65536 })`.\n00064| - Implement CSRF protection for state-changing operations. Use SameSite cookies or CSRF tokens. For Express, use `csurf` middleware. For Fastify, use `@fastify/csrf-protection`.\n00065| - Configure CORS properly: Allow only trusted origins. Never use `*` with credentials. Set specific origins: `{ origin: ['https://app.example.com'], credentials: true }`. Use `cors` middleware.\n00066| - Implement rate limiting per IP and per user. Use Redis-backed rate limiters: `express-rate-limit` with Redis store, or `@fastify/rate-limit`. Apply different limits to sensitive endpoints (login, signup).\n00067| - Prevent injection attacks: Use parameterized queries for SQL (never string concatenation). Use ORM query builders (Prisma, TypeORM). Validate input against allowlist patterns.\n00068| - Sanitize output for logs and responses. Never log passwords, tokens, credit cards. Implement redaction: `logger.info({ user: redact(user, ['password', 'ssn']) })`. Use `fast-redact` library.\n00069| - Implement Content Security Policy for served HTML: `helmet` middleware sets security headers. For crypto operations, use `node:crypto` module, never custom implementations.\n00071| - Implement secure session management: Rotate session IDs after login. Expire sessions after inactivity. Store sessions in Redis with TTL. Use `express-session` or `@fastify/secure-session`.\n00072| - Validate file uploads: Check file type (magic bytes, not extension), size limits, scan for malware. Store uploads outside web root. Use signed URLs for access (S3, CloudFront).\n00073| - Audit dependencies with `pnpm audit`, `npm audit`, or Socket.dev. Enable Dependabot/Renovate. Use Biome as faster alternative.\\n00012| - For monorepos, use pnpm workspaces with `workspace:*` protocol. Use Turborepo for build orchestration and caching. Structure as: `apps/`, `packages/`, `services/`.\\n00013| - Pin Node.js version with `.nvmrc` or `package.json` engines field. Use LTS versions (20.x or 22.x). Use Docker for consistent environments: `FROM node:22-alpine`.\\n00014| - Configure TypeScript with `skipLibCheck: true` for faster builds, `esModuleInterop: true` for CJS compatibility, `resolveJsonModule: true` for importing JSON configs.\\n00015| \\n00016| ## Error Handling\\n00017| \\n00018| - Never throw raw strings or objects. Always throw Error instances with codes: `throw new AppError('USER_NOT_FOUND', 'User not found', { userId })`. Include error codes for client handling.\\n00019| - Use discriminated unions for Result types in business logic: `type Result<T, E = Error> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: E }`. Prefer over throwing in pure functions.\\n00020| - Implement custom error hierarchy extending Error: `class ValidationError extends Error { constructor(message: string, public readonly field: string, public readonly code: string) { super(message); this.name = 'ValidationError'; Error.captureStackTrace(this, this.constructor); } }`.\\n00021| - Define domain-specific error types: `class DatabaseError`, `class AuthenticationError`, `class RateLimitError`. Include metadata for debugging: timestamp, request ID, user context.\\n00022| - Use `cause` property for error chaining (Node 16.9+): `throw new Error('Failed to create user', { cause: originalError })`. Preserves full error context through stack.\\n00023| - Implement global error handler middleware: Catch all errors, log with context, return sanitized responses. Never expose internal errors to clients: `{ code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', message: 'An error occurred' }`.\\n00024| - For HTTP APIs, map errors to status codes consistently: 400 (validation), 401 (auth), 403 (forbidden), 404 (not found), 409 (conflict), 429 (rate limit), 500 (internal). Use custom error mapper.\\n00025| - Validate external data at API boundaries with Zod schemas. Transform Zod errors into structured responses: `{ code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR', message: string, details: { field: string, message: string }[] }`.\\n00026| - Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient failures (database deadlocks, external APIs). Use `p-retry` library with jitter: `retry(() => fetchData(), { retries: 3, factor: 2 })`.\\n00027| - Use `never` return type for assertion functions: `function assertAuthenticated(user: User | null): asserts user is User { if (!user) throw new AuthError() }`. Narrows types after assertion.\\n00028| \\n00029| ## Async & Concurrency\\n00030| \\n00031| - Always use `async/await` over raw Promises. Use `Promise.all()` for parallel execution: `const [users, posts] = await Promise.all([db.users.findMany(), db.posts.findMany()])`. Never sequential awaits for independent operations.\\n00032| - Use `Promise.allSettled()` when you need all results regardless of failures. Use `Promise.race()` for timeout patterns: `Promise.race([fetchData(), timeout(5000)])`.\\n00033| - Implement proper cancellation with AbortController for HTTP requests, database queries: `const controller = new AbortController(); fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal }); setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 5000)`.\\n00034| - Use message queues (BullMQ, Bee-Queue) for background jobs and async processing. Define typed job payloads: `type EmailJob = { type: 'email'; to: string; template: string; data: Record<string, unknown> }`. Implement job retry and dead-letter queues.\\n00035| - Organize system into subsystems using message-passing architecture. Use EventEmitter or custom event bus for internal events. For complex workflows, use state machines with XState.\\n00036| - For CPU-intensive tasks, use worker threads (`node:worker_threads`). Communicate via `postMessage()` with typed messages. Use Piscina for worker pool management. Never block event loop.\\n00037| - Avoid shared state between requests. Use request-scoped context with AsyncLocalStorage: `const requestContext = new AsyncLocalStorage<{ requestId: string; userId?: string }>()`. Access in nested functions without passing explicitly.\\n00038| - Implement graceful shutdown: Listen for SIGTERM/SIGINT, stop accepting new connections, drain active requests, close database connections, flush logs. Use `@fastify/graceful-shutdown` or custom implementation.\\n00039| - Use streaming for large payloads: Node.js streams, async iterators. Process data in chunks to avoid memory issues: `for await (const chunk of readStream) { await processChunk(chunk) }`.\\n00040| - Handle uncaught errors: `process.on('uncaughtException')`, `process.on('unhandledRejection')`. Open circuit after threshold failures, prevent cascading failures. Use fallback responses during circuit open.\\n00043| \\n00044| ## Type Design & API\\n00045| \\n00046| - Use `interface` for object shapes that might be extended (DTOs, entities). Use `type` for unions, intersections, mapped types. Prefer `interface` for public APIs (better error messages).\\n00047| - Define API request/response types separately from domain models: `type CreateUserRequest = { email: string; name: string }`, `type UserResponse = { id: string; email: string; name: string; createdAt: string }`. Never expose internal models directly.\\n00048| - Use branded types for domain primitives: `type UserId = string & { readonly __brand: 'UserId' }; const makeUserId = (id: string): UserId => id as UserId`. Prevents mixing email with userId.\\n00049| - Use Zod for runtime validation and type inference: `const CreateUserSchema = z.object({ email: z.string().email(), name: z.string().min(1) }); type CreateUserDto = z.infer<typeof CreateUserSchema>`. Single source of truth.\\n00050| - Implement discriminated unions for polymorphic APIs: `type Event = { type: 'user.created'; userId: string } | { type: 'post.published'; postId: string }`. Use in event handlers, message queues.\\n00051| - Use template literal types for API routes: `type HttpMethod = 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'DELETE'; type ApiRoute = \\\\`/api/\\\\${string}\\\\`; type Endpoint<M extends HttpMethod> = { method: M; path: ApiRoute }`.\\n00052| - Define service interfaces with dependency injection in mind: `interface UserService { createUser(dto: CreateUserDto): Promise<User>; findById(id: UserId): Promise<User | null> }`. Always separate database models from API DTOs for loose coupling.\\n00058| \\n00059| ## Safety & Security\\n00060| \\n00061| - Validate and sanitize all external input at API boundaries. Use Zod schemas with transforms: `z.string().trim().toLowerCase()`. Never trust client input, query params, headers.\\n00062| - Implement authentication with JWT or session tokens. Enable `verbatimModuleSyntax` for explicit import/export control.\\n00006| - Always run build (`pnpm build`), tests (`pnpm test`), linter (`eslint --max-warnings 0`), and type-checker (`tsc --noEmit`) before finishing tasks.\\n00007| - Use `pnpm` over `npm` for faster installs and strict dependency resolution. Run `pnpm audit` and `pnpm outdated` regularly to check for vulnerabilities.\\n00008| - Configure `moduleResolution: \\\"bundler\\\"` or `\\\"node16\\\"` for Node.js projects. Use path aliases (`@/` for `src/`) in tsconfig and build config for clean imports.\\n00009| - Use `tsx` for running TypeScript directly in development: `tsx src/index.ts`. Use `tsup` or `esbuild` for production builds (faster than tsc). Configure source maps for debugging.\\n00010| - Enable `isolatedModules: true` for compatibility with fast transpilers. Avoid const enums and namespace merging patterns.\\n00011| - Use ESLint 9+ with flat config (`eslint.config.js`). Enable `@typescript-eslint/strict-type-checked` ruleset for backend code. Use Biome as faster alternative.\\n00012| - For monorepos, use pnpm workspaces with `workspace:*` protocol. Use Turborepo for build orchestration and caching. Structure as: `apps/`, `packages/`, `services/`.\\n00013| - Pin Node.js version with `.nvmrc` or `package.json` engines field. Use LTS versions (20.x or 22.x). Use Docker for consistent environments: `FROM node:22-alpine`.\\n00014| - Configure TypeScript with `skipLibCheck: true` for faster builds, `esModuleInterop: true` for CJS compatibility, `resolveJsonModule: true` for importing JSON configs.\\n00015| \\n00016| ## Error Handling\\n00017| \\n00018| - Never throw raw strings or objects. Always throw Error instances with codes: `throw new AppError('USER_NOT_FOUND', 'User not found', { userId })`. Include error codes for client handling.\\n00019| - Use discriminated unions for Result types in business logic: `type Result<T, E = Error> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: E }`. Prefer over throwing in pure functions.\\n00020| - Implement custom error hierarchy extending Error: `class ValidationError extends Error { constructor(message: string, public readonly field: string, public readonly code: string) { super(message); this.name = 'ValidationError'; Error.captureStackTrace(this, this.constructor); } }`.\\n00021| - Define domain-specific error types: `class DatabaseError`, `class AuthenticationError`, `class RateLimitError`. Include metadata for debugging: timestamp, request ID, user context.\\n00022| - Use `cause` property for error chaining (Node 16.9+): `throw new Error('Failed to create user', { cause: originalError })`. Preserves full error context through stack.\\n00023| - Implement global error handler middleware: Catch all errors, log with context, return sanitized responses. Never expose internal errors to clients: `{ code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', message: 'An error occurred' }`.\\n00024| - For HTTP APIs, map errors to status codes consistently: 400 (validation), 401 (auth), 403 (forbidden), 404 (not found), 409 (conflict), 429 (rate limit), 500 (internal). Use custom error mapper.\\n00025| - Validate external data at API boundaries with Zod schemas. Transform Zod errors into structured responses: `{ code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR', message: string, details: { field: string, message: string }[] }`.\\n00026| - Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient failures (database deadlocks, external APIs). Use `p-retry` library with jitter: `retry(() => fetchData(), { retries: 3, factor: 2 })`.\\n00027| - Use `never` return type for assertion functions: `function assertAuthenticated(user: User | null): asserts user is User { if (!user) throw new AuthError() }`. Narrows types after assertion.\\n00028| \\n00029| ## Async & Concurrency\\n00030| \\n00031| - Always use `async/await` over raw Promises. Use `Promise.all()` for parallel execution: `const [users, posts] = await Promise.all([db.users.findMany(), db.posts.findMany()])`. Never sequential awaits for independent operations.\\n00032| - Use `Promise.allSettled()` when you need all results regardless of failures. Use `Promise.race()` for timeout patterns: `Promise.race([fetchData(), timeout(5000)])`.\\n00033| - Implement proper cancellation with AbortController for HTTP requests, database queries: `const controller = new AbortController(); fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal }); setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 5000)`.\\n00034| - Use message queues (BullMQ, Bee-Queue) for background jobs and async processing. Define typed job payloads: `type EmailJob = { type: 'email'; to: string; template: string; data: Record<string, unknown> }`. Implement job retry and dead-letter queues.\\n00035| - Organize system into subsystems using message-passing architecture. Use EventEmitter or custom event bus for internal events. For complex workflows, use state machines with XState.\\n00036| - For CPU-intensive tasks, use worker threads (`node:worker_threads`). Communicate via `postMessage()` with typed messages. Use Piscina for worker pool management. Never block event loop.\\n00037| - Avoid shared state between requests. Use request-scoped context with AsyncLocalStorage: `const requestContext = new AsyncLocalStorage<{ requestId: string; userId?: string }>()`. Access in nested functions without passing explicitly.\\n00038| - Implement graceful shutdown: Listen for SIGTERM/SIGINT, stop accepting new connections, drain active requests, close database connections, flush logs. Use `@fastify/graceful-shutdown` or custom implementation.\\n00039| - Use streaming for large payloads: Node.js streams, async iterators. Process data in chunks to avoid memory issues: `for await (const chunk of readStream) { await processChunk(chunk) }`.\\n00040| - Handle uncaught errors: `process.on('uncaughtException')`, `process.on('unhandledRejection')`. Log error, clean up resources, gracefully exit. Use process managers (PM2, Kubernetes) for restart.\\n00041| - Use connection pooling for databases (Prisma, TypeORM), Redis, HTTP clients. Configure pool size based on workload: Start with `max: 10`, tune based on monitoring.\\n00042| - Implement circuit breakers for external dependencies using `opossum`. Open circuit after threshold failures, prevent cascading failures. Use fallback responses during circuit open.\\n00043| \\n00044| ## Type Design & API\\n00045| \\n00046| - Use `interface` for object shapes that might be extended (DTOs, entities). Use `type` for unions, intersections, mapped types. Prefer `interface` for public APIs (better error messages).\\n00047| - Define API request/response types separately from domain models: `type CreateUserRequest = { email: string; name: string }`, `type UserResponse = { id: string; email: string; name: string; createdAt: string }`. Never expose internal models directly.\\n00048| - Use branded types for domain primitives: `type UserId = string & { readonly __brand: 'UserId' }; const makeUserId = (id: string): UserId => id as UserId`. Prevents mixing email with userId.\\n00049| - Use Zod for runtime validation and type inference: `const CreateUserSchema = z.object({ email: z.string().email(), name: z.string().min(1) }); type CreateUserDto = z.infer<typeof CreateUserSchema>`. Single source of truth.\\n00050| - Implement discriminated unions for polymorphic APIs: `type Event = { type: 'user.created'; userId: string } | { type: 'post.published'; postId: string }`. Use in event handlers, message queues.\\n00051| - Use template literal types for API routes: `type HttpMethod = 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'DELETE'; type ApiRoute = \\\\`/api/\\\\${string}\\\\`; type Endpoint<M extends HttpMethod> = { method: M; path: ApiRoute }`.\\n00052| - Define service interfaces with dependency injection in mind: `interface UserService { createUser(dto: CreateUserDto): Promise<User>; findById(id: UserId): Promise<User | null> }`. Easy to mock, test, replace implementations.\\n00053| - Use generic constraints for type-safe query builders: `function where<T, K extends keyof T>(field: K, value: T[K]): Query<T>`. Ensures field exists and value matches type.\\n00054| - Use utility types extensively: `Omit<User, 'password'>` for public user type, `Partial<User>` for update DTOs, `Pick<User, 'id' | 'email'>` for minimal representations.\\n00055| - Implement builder pattern for complex objects: `class QueryBuilder<T> { where(field: keyof T, value: unknown): this; orderBy(field: keyof T): this; build(): Query<T> }`. Fluent API with type safety.\\n00056| - Use const type parameters (TS 5.0+) for preserving literal types: `function createRoute<const T extends string>(path: T): Route<T>`. Useful for type-safe routing.\\n00057| - Define database models with ORM types: For Prisma, use generated types. For custom ORMs, define entity interfaces. Always separate database models from API DTOs for loose coupling.\\n00058| \\n00059| ## Safety & Security\\n00060| \\n00061| - Validate and sanitize all external input at API boundaries. Use Zod schemas with transforms: `z.string().trim().toLowerCase()`. Never trust client input, query params, headers.\\n00062| - Implement authentication with JWT or session tokens. Store tokens in httpOnly, secure, SameSite=Strict cookies. For APIs, use Authorization header: `Bearer <token>`. Validate signature and expiration.\\n00063| - Use bcrypt or argon2 for password hashing. Never store plain text passwords. Use high cost factor: `bcrypt.hash(password, 12)` or `argon2.hash(password, { timeCost: 3, memoryCost: 65536 })`.\\n00064| - Implement CSRF protection for state-changing operations. Use SameSite cookies or CSRF tokens. For Express, use `csurf` middleware. For Fastify, use `@fastify/csrf-protection`.\\n00065| - Configure CORS properly: Allow only trusted origins. Never use `*` with credentials. Set specific origins: `{ origin: ['https://app.example.com'], credentials: true }`. Use `cors` middleware.\\n00066| - Implement rate limiting per IP and per user. Use Redis-backed rate limiters: `express-rate-limit` with Redis store, or `@fastify/rate-limit`. Apply different limits to sensitive endpoints (login, signup).\\n00067| - Prevent injection attacks: Use parameterized queries for SQL (never string concatenation). Use ORM query builders (Prisma, TypeORM). Validate input against allowlist patterns.\\n00068| - Sanitize output for logs and responses. Never log passwords, tokens, credit cards. Implement redaction: `logger.info({ user: redact(user, ['password', 'ssn']) })`. Use `fast-redact` library.\\n00069| - Implement Content Security Policy for served HTML: `helmet` middleware sets security headers. Configure CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options.\\n00070| - Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual()` for comparing secrets (tokens, signatures). Prevents timing attacks. For crypto operations, use `node:crypto` module, never custom implementations.\\n00071| - Implement secure session management: Rotate session IDs after login. Expire sessions after inactivity. Store sessions in Redis with TTL. Use `express-session` or `@fastify/secure-session`.\\n00072| - Validate file uploads: Check file type (magic bytes, not extension), size limits, scan for malware. Store uploads outside web root. Use signed URLs for access (S3, CloudFront).\\n00073| - Audit dependencies with `pnpm audit`, `npm audit`, or Socket.dev. Enable Dependabot/Renovate. Review new dependencies for supply chain attacks. Use `socket npm install` for security analysis.\\n00074| - Implement security headers: Use `helmet` middleware. Enable HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin.\\n00075| \\n00076| ## Serialization & Data\\n00077| \\n00078| - Use Zod for runtime validation of API requests and external data: `const parsed = CreateUserSchema.parse(req.body)`. Throws on validation failure with detailed errors.\\n00079| - Transform Zod validation errors into user-friendly API responses: `.safeParse()` returns Result type. Map errors: `error.issues.map(i => ({ field: i.path.join('.'), message: i.message }))`.\\n00080| - Serialize dates as ISO 8601 strings in JSON responses: `JSON.stringify({ createdAt: new Date().toISOString() })`. Define serializers for custom types: Use `superjson` for Date, Map, Set, BigInt, RegExp.\\n00081| - Implement DTO transformers: Map database models to API responses. Exclude sensitive fields (password, internal IDs). Use class-transformer or manual mappers: `function toUserResponse(user: User): UserResponse { return { id: user.id, email: user.email } }`.\\n00082| - Use Prisma for type-safe database access. Define schema in `schema.prisma`, generate types with `prisma generate`. Use relations, transactions, middleware for business logic.\\n00083| - Implement database migrations: Use Prisma Migrate, TypeORM migrations, or Knex. Version migrations, test rollbacks. Never modify production schema manually.\\n00084| - Handle pagination with cursor-based approach for large datasets: `{ data: T[], nextCursor: string | null, hasMore: boolean }`. Or use Zod and generate JSON Schema: `zodToJsonSchema()`.\\n00086| - Implement ETags for cache validation: Hash response body, set ETag header. Check `If-None-Match`, return 304 if match. Smaller payloads, faster serialization than JSON.\\n00088| - Handle BigInt serialization: JSON.stringify doesn't support BigInt. Use custom replacer: `JSON.stringify(obj, (key, value) => typeof value === 'bigint' ? value.toString() : value)` or use `json-bigint` library.\\n00089| - Implement database query result caching: Use Redis for frequently accessed data. Define TTL per entity type. Invalidate on updates: `await redis.del(\\\\`user:\\\\${userId}\\\\`)`.\\n00090| \\n00091| ## Testing\\n00092| \\n00093| - Use Vitest over Jest for modern projects (faster, native ESM, better TypeScript support). Verify proper locking or optimistic locking.\\n00105| \\n00106| ## Logging & Observability\\n00107| \\n00108| - Use Pino for structured logging (fastest JSON logger for Node.js). Create middleware to inject context: `req.log = logger.child({ requestId: uuid(), userId: req.user?.id })`.\\n00111| - Log structured data with fields: `logger.info({ userId, action: 'user.created', duration: 123 }, 'User created successfully')`. Redact sensitive data (tokens, passwords, SSN) in production logs. Track business metrics (signups, orders, revenue) alongside technical metrics. Create dashboards for observability.\\n00120| \\n00121| ## Performance\\n00122| \\n00123| - Profile before optimizing: Use Node.js built-in profiler (`node --prof`), Chrome DevTools (inspect mode), or `clinic.js` for flame graphs, heap analysis, event loop analysis.\\n00124| - Optimize database queries: Use indexes on frequently queried fields. Avoid N+1 queries (use joins or dataloader). Use `EXPLAIN` to analyze query plans. Add pagination to large result sets.\\n00125| - Implement caching strategy: Cache frequently accessed data in Redis with TTL. Use cache-aside pattern: Check cache, miss → fetch from DB → set cache. Define cache key convention: `entity:id`.\\n00126| - Use connection pooling: Configure database pool size based on workload. For Prisma: `connection_limit` in database URL. For Redis: `ioredis` with pool. Monitor pool exhaustion.\\n00127| - Optimize JSON serialization: Use `fast-json-stringify` with JSON Schema for 2-3x faster serialization. For large responses, use streaming: `res.write()` chunks instead of single `res.json()`.\\n00128| - Implement response compression: Use `compression` middleware (gzip, brotli). Configure level vs speed tradeoff. Enable for text responses (JSON, HTML), skip for images, video.\\n00129| - Use clustering for CPU utilization: Node.js is single-threaded. Use `cluster` module to spawn workers per CPU core. Or deploy multiple instances behind load balancer (better for containers).\\n00130| - Optimize cold starts: Minimize startup work. Lazy load heavy dependencies. Use `import()` for conditional imports. For serverless (AWS Lambda), reduce bundle size, use provisioned concurrency.\\n00131| - Implement request coalescing: Deduplicate concurrent identical requests (e.g., same user requesting same resource multiple times). Use in-memory Map to track pending requests.\\n00132| - Use async iterators for streaming large datasets: `async function* fetchUsers() { for (const batch of batches) { yield* batch } }`. Process in chunks to avoid loading entire dataset in memory.\\n00133| - Monitor event loop lag: Use `toobusy-js` or custom monitoring: `const start = Date.now(); setImmediate(() => { const lag = Date.now() - start })`. Alert when lag exceeds threshold (indicates blocked event loop).\\n00134| - Optimize Docker images: Use multi-stage builds. Use alpine base image. Copy only production dependencies: `pnpm install --prod`. Remove dev dependencies and cache. Use `.dockerignore`.\\n00135| \\n00136| ## Dependencies\\n00137| \\n00138| - Minimize dependencies: Each adds bundle size, security risk, maintenance burden. Evaluate necessity before adding. Implement simple utilities instead of adding library (e.g., retry logic vs full library).\\n00139| - Audit dependencies before adding: Check npm downloads, GitHub stars, last update date, open issues, security advisories. Use `npx socket npm install <package>` for security analysis. Avoid packages with install scripts.\\n00140| - Pin exact versions in package.json for applications: Use `\\\"fastify\\\": \\\"5.2.0\\\"` not `\\\"^5.2.0\\\"`. Avoid packages requiring manual type definitions.\\n00142| - Use workspace dependencies in monorepos: Define in `[workspace.dependencies]` in root package.json. Use `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in CI/production to ensure reproducible builds. Never use `npm update` without testing.\\n00148| \\n00149| ## Documentation\\n00150| \\n00151| - Write TSDoc comments for exported functions, classes, types: `/** Creates a new user. @param dto - User creation data. @returns Created user with generated ID. @throws {ValidationError} When email is invalid. @example \\\\`\\\\`\\\\`ts\\\\nawait createUser({ email: 'user@example.com', name: 'John' })\\\\n\\\\`\\\\`\\\\` */`.\\n00152| - Document API endpoints with OpenAPI/Swagger: Use `@fastify/swagger` or `swagger-jsdoc`. Document table purposes, indexes, constraints. Explain complex queries or stored procedures. Use `prisma-docs` or `dbdocs.io`.\\n00161| \\n00162| ## Code Style\\n00163| \\n00164| - Use functional programming principles: Pure functions, immutability, composition. Avoid mutations: Use `map/filter/reduce` over `for` loops modifying arrays. Use spread operator: `{ ...obj, key: newValue }`.\\n00165| - Follow naming conventions: `camelCase` for variables/functions, `PascalCase` for types/interfaces/classes, `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` for constants. Use descriptive names: `fetchUserById` not `getUser`.\\n00166| - Keep functions small and focused: <50 lines ideally. Single responsibility. Extract complex logic into well-named helper functions. Use early returns: `if (!user) return null;`.\\n00167| - Order imports consistently: Node.js built-ins first (`node:fs`, `node:path`), external dependencies second (alphabetically), internal modules third (`@/services/*`), types fourth. Use auto-sorting with `eslint-plugin-import`.\\n00168| - Use const by default, let only when reassignment needed. Never use var. Use destructuring: `const { id, email } = user` not `const id = user.id`.\\n00169| - Prefer arrow functions for callbacks and inline functions: `const double = (x: number) => x * 2`. Use function declarations for top-level exported functions, methods.\\n00170| - Use template literals for string interpolation: `` `User ${id} not found` `` not `'User ' + id + ' not found'`. Use template literals for multi-line strings, SQL queries.\\n00171| - Avoid nested ternaries. Use if/else or extract to functions. Max one ternary per line: `const status = isActive ? 'active' : 'inactive'`. For multiple conditions, use switch or object lookup.\\n00172| - Use optional chaining: `user?.profile?.avatar` instead of `user && user.profile && user.profile.avatar`. Use nullish coalescing: `value ?? defaultValue` (handles `0`, `''`, `false` correctly).\\n00173| - Export functions as named exports: `export async function createUser(dto: CreateUserDto): Promise<User>`. Better for tree-shaking, refactoring. Use default exports sparingly (e.g., Express app).\\n00174| - Use trailing commas in multi-line arrays, objects, function parameters: Cleaner git diffs, easier to reorder lines. Prettier enforces this with `trailingComma: 'all'`.\\n00175| - Organize files consistently: Imports → Constants → Types → Functions → Exports. Group related functions. Use barrel exports (`index.ts`) for clean imports: `import { createUser, findUser } from '@/services/user'`.\\n00176| - Use async/await consistently. Never mix promises and callbacks. TypeScript Backend Development Guidelines\\n00002| \\n00003| ## Toolchain & Build\\n00004| \\n00005| - Always use TypeScript 5.7+ with `strict: true`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true`, and `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true` in tsconfig.json. Enable `verbatimModuleSyntax` for explicit import/export control.\\n00006| - Always run build (`pnpm build`), tests (`pnpm test`), linter (`eslint --max-warnings 0`), and type-checker (`tsc --noEmit`) before finishing tasks.\\n00007| - Use `pnpm` over `npm` for faster installs and strict dependency resolution. Run `pnpm audit` and `pnpm outdated` regularly to check for vulnerabilities.\\n00008| - Configure `moduleResolution: \\\"bundler\\\"` or `\\\"node16\\\"` for Node.js projects. Use path aliases (`@/` for `src/`) in tsconfig and build config for clean imports.\\n00009| - Use `tsx` for running TypeScript directly in development: `tsx src/index.ts`. Use `tsup` or `esbuild` for production builds (faster than tsc). Configure source maps for debugging.\\n00010| - Enable `isolatedModules: true` for compatibility with fast transpilers. Avoid const enums and namespace merging patterns.\\n00011| - Use ESLint 9+ with flat config (`eslint.config.js`). Enable `@typescript-eslint/strict-type-checked` ruleset for backend code. Use Biome as faster alternative.\\n00012| - For monorepos, use pnpm workspaces with `workspace:*` protocol. Use Turborepo for build orchestration and caching. Structure as: `apps/`, `packages/`, `services/`.\\n00013| - Pin Node.js version with `.nvmrc` or `package.json` engines field. Use LTS versions (20.x or 22.x). Use Docker for consistent environments: `FROM node:22-alpine`.\\n00014| - Configure TypeScript with `skipLibCheck: true` for faster builds, `esModuleInterop: true` for CJS compatibility, `resolveJsonModule: true` for importing JSON configs.\\n00015| \\n00016| ## Error Handling\\n00017| \\n00018| - Never throw raw strings or objects. Always throw Error instances with codes: `throw new AppError('USER_NOT_FOUND', 'User not found', { userId })`. Include error codes for client handling.\\n00019| - Use discriminated unions for Result types in business logic: `type Result<T, E = Error> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: E }`. Prefer over throwing in pure functions.\\n00020| - Implement custom error hierarchy extending Error: `class ValidationError extends Error { constructor(message: string, public readonly field: string, public readonly code: string) { super(message); this.name = 'ValidationError'; Error.captureStackTrace(this, this.constructor); } }`.\\n00021| - Define domain-specific error types: `class DatabaseError`, `class AuthenticationError`, `class RateLimitError`. Include metadata for debugging: timestamp, request ID, user context.\\n00022| - Use `cause` property for error chaining (Node 16.9+): `throw new Error('Failed to create user', { cause: originalError })`. Preserves full error context through stack.\\n00023| - Implement global error handler middleware: Catch all errors, log with context, return sanitized responses. Never expose internal errors to clients: `{ code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', message: 'An error occurred' }`.\\n00024| - For HTTP APIs, map errors to status codes consistently: 400 (validation), 401 (auth), 403 (forbidden), 404 (not found), 409 (conflict), 429 (rate limit), 500 (internal). Use custom error mapper.\\n00025| - Validate external data at API boundaries with Zod schemas. Transform Zod errors into structured responses: `{ code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR', message: string, details: { field: string, message: string }[] }`.\\n00026| - Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient failures (database deadlocks, external APIs). Use `p-retry` library with jitter: `retry(() => fetchData(), { retries: 3, factor: 2 })`.\\n00027| - Use `never` return type for assertion functions: `function assertAuthenticated(user: User | null): asserts user is User { if (!user) throw new AuthError() }`. Narrows types after assertion.\\n00028| \\n00029| ## Async & Concurrency\\n00030| \\n00031| - Always use `async/await` over raw Promises. Use `Promise.all()` for parallel execution: `const [users, posts] = await Promise.all([db.users.findMany(), db.posts.findMany()])`. Never sequential awaits for independent operations.\\n00032| - Use `Promise.allSettled()` when you need all results regardless of failures. Use `Promise.race()` for timeout patterns: `Promise.race([fetchData(), timeout(5000)])`.\\n00033| - Implement proper cancellation with AbortController for HTTP requests, database queries: `const controller = new AbortController(); fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal }); setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 5000)`.\\n00034| - Use message queues (BullMQ, Bee-Queue) for background jobs and async processing. Define typed job payloads: `type EmailJob = { type: 'email'; to: string; template: string; data: Record<string, unknown> }`. Implement job retry and dead-letter queues.\\n00035| - Organize system into subsystems using message-passing architecture. Use EventEmitter or custom event bus for internal events. For complex workflows, use state machines with XState.\\n00036| - For CPU-intensive tasks, use worker threads (`node:worker_threads`). Communicate via `postMessage()` with typed messages. Use Piscina for worker pool management. Never block event loop.\\n00037| - Avoid shared state between requests. Use request-scoped context with AsyncLocalStorage: `const requestContext = new AsyncLocalStorage<{ requestId: string; userId?: string }>()`. Always throw Error instances with codes: `throw new AppError('USER_NOT_FOUND', 'User not found', { userId })`. Include error codes for client handling.\\n00019| - Use discriminated unions for Result types in business logic: `type Result<T, E = Error> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: E }`. Prefer over throwing in pure functions.\\n00020| - Implement custom error hierarchy extending Error: `class ValidationError extends Error { constructor(message: string, public readonly field: string, public readonly code: string) { super(message); this.name = 'ValidationError'; Error.captureStackTrace(this, this.constructor); } }`.\\n00021| - Define domain-specific error types: `class DatabaseError`, `class AuthenticationError`, `class RateLimitError`. Include metadata for debugging: timestamp, request ID, user context.\\n00022| - Use `cause` property for error chaining (Node 16.9+): `throw new Error('Failed to create user', { cause: originalError })`. Preserves full error context through stack.\\n00023| - Implement global error handler middleware: Catch all errors, log with context, return sanitized responses. Never expose internal errors to clients: `{ code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', message: 'An error occurred' }`.\\n00024| - For HTTP APIs, map errors to status codes consistently: 400 (validation), 401 (auth), 403 (forbidden), 404 (not found), 409 (conflict), 429 (rate limit), 500 (internal). Use custom error mapper.\\n00025| - Validate external data at API boundaries with Zod schemas. Use `p-retry` library with jitter: `retry(() => fetchData(), { retries: 3, factor: 2 })`.\\n00027| - Use `never` return type for assertion functions: `function assertAuthenticated(user: User | null): asserts user is User { if (!user) throw new AuthError() }`. Never sequential awaits for independent operations.\\n00032| - Use `Promise.allSettled()` when you need all results regardless of failures. Use `Promise.race()` for timeout patterns: `Promise.race([fetchData(), timeout(5000)])`.\\n00033| - Implement proper cancellation with AbortController for HTTP requests, database queries: `const controller = new AbortController(); fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal }); setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 5000)`.\\n00034| - Use message queues (BullMQ, Bee-Queue) for background jobs and async processing. Enable `verbatimModuleSyntax` for explicit import/export control.\n00006| - Always run build (`pnpm build`), tests (`pnpm test`), linter (`eslint --max-warnings 0`), and type-checker (`tsc --noEmit`) before finishing tasks.\n00007| - Use `pnpm` over `npm` for faster installs and strict dependency resolution. Run `pnpm audit` and `pnpm outdated` regularly to check for vulnerabilities.\n00008| - Configure `moduleResolution: \"bundler\"` or `\"node16\"` for Node.js projects. Use path aliases (`@/` for `src/`) in tsconfig and build config for clean imports.\n00009| - Use `tsx` for running TypeScript directly in development: `tsx src/index.ts`. Use `tsup` or `esbuild` for production builds (faster than tsc). Configure source maps for debugging.\n00010| - Enable `isolatedModules: true` for compatibility with fast transpilers. Avoid const enums and namespace merging patterns.\n00011| - Use ESLint 9+ with flat config (`eslint.config.js`). Enable `@typescript-eslint/strict-type-checked` ruleset for backend code. Use Biome as faster alternative.\n00012| - For monorepos, use pnpm workspaces with `workspace:*` protocol. Use Turborepo for build orchestration and caching. Structure as: `apps/`, `packages/`, `services/`.\n00013| - Pin Node.js version with `.nvmrc` or `package.json` engines field. Use LTS versions (20.x or 22.x). Use Docker for consistent environments: `FROM node:22-alpine`.\n00014| - Configure TypeScript with `skipLibCheck: true` for faster builds, `esModuleInterop: true` for CJS compatibility, `resolveJsonModule: true` for importing JSON configs.\n00015| \n00016| ## Error Handling\n00017| \n00018| - Never throw raw strings or objects. Always throw Error instances with codes: `throw new AppError('USER_NOT_FOUND', 'User not found', { userId })`. Include error codes for client handling.\n00019| - Use discriminated unions for Result types in business logic: `type Result<T, E = Error> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: E }`. Prefer over throwing in pure functions.\n00020| - Implement custom error hierarchy extending Error: `class ValidationError extends Error { constructor(message: string, public readonly field: string, public readonly code: string) { super(message); this.name = 'ValidationError'; Error.captureStackTrace(this, this.constructor); } }`.\n00021| - Define domain-specific error types: `class DatabaseError`, `class AuthenticationError`, `class RateLimitError`. Include metadata for debugging: timestamp, request ID, user context.\n00022| - Use `cause` property for error chaining (Node 16.9+): `throw new Error('Failed to create user', { cause: originalError })`. Preserves full error context through stack.\n00023| - Implement global error handler middleware: Catch all errors, log with context, return sanitized responses. Never expose internal errors to clients: `{ code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', message: 'An error occurred' }`.\n00024| - For HTTP APIs, map errors to status codes consistently: 400 (validation), 401 (auth), 403 (forbidden), 404 (not found), 409 (conflict), 429 (rate limit), 500 (internal). Use custom error mapper.\n00025| - Validate external data at API boundaries with Zod schemas. Transform Zod errors into structured responses: `{ code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR', message: string, details: { field: string, message: string }[] }`.\n00026| - Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient failures (database deadlocks, external APIs). Use `p-retry` library with jitter: `retry(() => fetchData(), { retries: 3, factor: 2 })`.\n00027| - Use `never` return type for assertion functions: `function assertAuthenticated(user: User | null): asserts user is User { if (!user) throw new AuthError() }`. Narrows types after assertion.\n00028| \n00029| ## Async & Concurrency\n00030| \n00031| - Always use `async/await` over raw Promises. Use `Promise.all()` for parallel execution: `const [users, posts] = await Promise.all([db.users.findMany(), db.posts.findMany()])`. Never sequential awaits for independent operations.\n00032| - Use `Promise.allSettled()` when you need all results regardless of failures. Use `Promise.race()` for timeout patterns: `Promise.race([fetchData(), timeout(5000)])`.\n00033| - Implement proper cancellation with AbortController for HTTP requests, database queries: `const controller = new AbortController(); fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal }); setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 5000)`.\n00034| - Use message queues (BullMQ, Bee-Queue) for background jobs and async processing. Define typed job payloads: `type EmailJob = { type: 'email'; to: string; template: string; data: Record<string, unknown> }`. Implement job retry and dead-letter queues.\n00035| - Organize system into subsystems using message-passing architecture. Use EventEmitter or custom event bus for internal events. For complex workflows, use state machines with XState.\n00036| - For CPU-intensive tasks, use worker threads (`node:worker_threads`). Communicate via `postMessage()` with typed messages. Use Piscina for worker pool management. Never block event loop.\n00037| - Avoid shared state between requests. Use request-scoped context with AsyncLocalStorage: `const requestContext = new AsyncLocalStorage<{ requestId: string; userId?: string }>()`. Access in nested functions without passing explicitly.\n00038| - Implement graceful shutdown: Listen for SIGTERM/SIGINT, stop accepting new connections, drain active requests, close database connections, flush logs. Use `@fastify/graceful-shutdown` or custom implementation.\n00039| - Use streaming for large payloads: Node.js streams, async iterators. Process data in chunks to avoid memory issues: `for await (const chunk of readStream) { await processChunk(chunk) }`.\n00040| - Handle uncaught errors: `process.on('uncaughtException')`, `process.on('unhandledRejection')`. Log error, clean up resources, gracefully exit. Use process managers (PM2, Kubernetes) for restart.\n00041| - Use connection pooling for databases (Prisma, TypeORM), Redis, HTTP clients. Configure pool size based on workload: Start with `max: 10`, tune based on monitoring.\n00042| - Implement circuit breakers for external dependencies using `opossum`. Open circuit after threshold failures, prevent cascading failures. Use fallback responses during circuit open.\n00043| \n00044| ## Type Design & API\n00045| \n00046| - Use `interface` for object shapes that might be extended (DTOs, entities). Use `type` for unions, intersections, mapped types. Prefer `interface` for public APIs (better error messages).\n00047| - Define API request/response types separately from domain models: `type CreateUserRequest = { email: string; name: string }`, `type UserResponse = { id: string; email: string; name: string; createdAt: string }`. Never expose internal models directly.\n00048| - Use branded types for domain primitives: `type UserId = string & { readonly __brand: 'UserId' }; const makeUserId = (id: string): UserId => id as UserId`. Prevents mixing email with userId.\n00049| - Use Zod for runtime validation and type inference: `const CreateUserSchema = z.object({ email: z.string().email(), name: z.string().min(1) }); type CreateUserDto = z.infer<typeof CreateUserSchema>`. Single source of truth.\n00050| - Implement discriminated unions for polymorphic APIs: `type Event = { type: 'user.created'; userId: string } | { type: 'post.published'; postId: string }`. Use in event handlers, message queues.\n00051| - Use template literal types for API routes: `type HttpMethod = 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'DELETE'; type ApiRoute = \\`/api/\\${string}\\`; type Endpoint<M extends HttpMethod> = { method: M; path: ApiRoute }`.\n00052| - Define service interfaces with dependency injection in mind: `interface UserService { createUser(dto: CreateUserDto): Promise<User>; findById(id: UserId): Promise<User | null> }`. Easy to mock, test, replace implementations.\n00053| - Use generic constraints for type-safe query builders: `function where<T, K extends keyof T>(field: K, value: T[K]): Query<T>`. Ensures field exists and value matches type.\n00054| - Use utility types extensively: `Omit<User, 'password'>` for public user type, `Partial<User>` for update DTOs, `Pick<User, 'id' | 'email'>` for minimal representations.\n00055| - Implement builder pattern for complex objects: `class QueryBuilder<T> { where(field: keyof T, value: unknown): this; orderBy(field: keyof T): this; build(): Query<T> }`. Fluent API with type safety.\n00056| - Use const type parameters (TS 5.0+) for preserving literal types: `function createRoute<const T extends string>(path: T): Route<T>`. Useful for type-safe routing.\n00057| - Define database models with ORM types: For Prisma, use generated types. For custom ORMs, define entity interfaces. Always separate database models from API DTOs for loose coupling.\n00058| \n00059| ## Safety & Security\n00060| \n00061| - Validate and sanitize all external input at API boundaries. Use Zod schemas with transforms: `z.string().trim().toLowerCase()`. Never trust client input, query params, headers.\n00062| - Implement authentication with JWT or session tokens. Store tokens in httpOnly, secure, SameSite=Strict cookies. For APIs, use Authorization header: `Bearer <token>`. Validate signature and expiration.\n00063| - Use bcrypt or argon2 for password hashing. Never store plain text passwords. Use high cost factor: `bcrypt.hash(password, 12)` or `argon2.hash(password, { timeCost: 3, memoryCost: 65536 })`.\n00064| - Implement CSRF protection for state-changing operations. Use SameSite cookies or CSRF tokens. For Express, use `csurf` middleware. For Fastify, use `@fastify/csrf-protection`.\n00065| - Configure CORS properly: Allow only trusted origins. Never use `*` with credentials. Set specific origins: `{ origin: ['https://app.example.com'], credentials: true }`. Use `cors` middleware.\n00066| - Implement rate limiting per IP and per user. Use Redis-backed rate limiters: `express-rate-limit` with Redis store, or `@fastify/rate-limit`. Apply different limits to sensitive endpoints (login, signup).\n00067| - Prevent injection attacks: Use parameterized queries for SQL (never string concatenation). Use ORM query builders (Prisma, TypeORM). Validate input against allowlist patterns.\n00068| - Sanitize output for logs and responses. Never log passwords, tokens, credit cards. Implement redaction: `logger.info({ user: redact(user, ['password', 'ssn']) })`. Use `fast-redact` library.\n00069| - Implement Content Security Policy for served HTML: `helmet` middleware sets security headers. Configure CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options.\n00070| - Use `crypto.timingSafeEqual()` for comparing secrets (tokens, signatures). Prevents timing attacks. For crypto operations, use `node:crypto` module, never custom implementations.\n00071| - Implement secure session management: Rotate session IDs after login. Expire sessions after inactivity. Store sessions in Redis with TTL. Use `express-session` or `@fastify/secure-session`.\n00072| - Validate file uploads: Check file type (magic bytes, not extension), size limits, scan for malware. Store uploads outside web root. Use signed URLs for access (S3, CloudFront).\n00073| - Audit dependencies with `pnpm audit`, `npm audit`, or Socket.dev. Enable Dependabot/Renovate. Review new dependencies for supply chain attacks. Use `socket npm install` for security analysis.\n00074| - Implement security headers: Use `helmet` middleware. Enable HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin.\n00075| \n00076| ## Serialization & Data\n00077| \n00078| - Use Zod for runtime validation of API requests and external data: `const parsed = CreateUserSchema.parse(req.body)`. Throws on validation failure with detailed errors.\n00079| - Transform Zod validation errors into user-friendly API responses: `.safeParse()` returns Result type. Map errors: `error.issues.map(i => ({ field: i.path.join('.'), message: i.message }))`.\n00080| - Serialize dates as ISO 8601 strings in JSON responses: `JSON.stringify({ createdAt: new Date().toISOString() })`. Define serializers for custom types: Use `superjson` for Date, Map, Set, BigInt, RegExp.\n00081| - Implement DTO transformers: Map database models to API responses. Exclude sensitive fields (password, internal IDs). Use class-transformer or manual mappers: `function toUserResponse(user: User): UserResponse { return { id: user.id, email: user.email } }`.\n00082| - Use Prisma for type-safe database access. Define schema in `schema.prisma`, generate types with `prisma generate`. Use relations, transactions, middleware for business logic.\n00083| - Implement database migrations: Use Prisma Migrate, TypeORM migrations, or Knex. Version migrations, test rollbacks. Smaller payloads, faster serialization than JSON.\n00088| - Handle BigInt serialization: JSON.stringify doesn't support BigInt. Use custom replacer: `JSON.stringify(obj, (key, value) => typeof value === 'bigint' ? value.toString() : value)` or use `json-bigint` library.\n00089| - Implement database query result caching: Use Redis for frequently accessed data. Define TTL per entity type. Invalidate on updates: `await redis.del(\\`user:\\${userId}\\`)`.\n00090| \n00091| ## Testing\n00092| \n00093| - Use Vitest over Jest for modern projects (faster, native ESM, better TypeScript support). Use `@faker-js/faker` for generating realistic test data.\n00097| - Mock external dependencies (third-party APIs, email services) with MSW (Mock Service Worker) for HTTP or `vi.mock()` for modules. Test across different databases, environments. Run in CI with Docker Compose: database, Redis, app.\n00103| - Aim for 80%+ coverage on business logic. Verify proper locking or optimistic locking.\n00105| \n00106| ## Logging & Observability\n00107| \n00108| - Use Pino for structured logging (fastest JSON logger for Node.js). Check database connectivity, Redis, external dependencies. Use PagerDuty, Opsgenie, or cloud provider alerts. Define SLOs and alert on SLO violations.\n00118| - Use structured logs for audit trail: Log all state-changing operations (create, update, delete) with actor, timestamp, old/new values. Store in separate audit log table or log aggregation service.\n00119| - Collect and analyze metrics: Use Datadog, New Relic, Prometheus + Grafana. Track business metrics (signups, orders, revenue) alongside technical metrics. Create dashboards for observability.\n00120| \n00121| ## Performance\n00122| \n00123| - Profile before optimizing: Use Node.js built-in profiler (`node --prof`), Chrome DevTools (inspect mode), or `clinic.js` for flame graphs, heap analysis, event loop analysis.\n00124| - Optimize database queries: Use indexes on frequently queried fields. Avoid N+1 queries (use joins or dataloader). Use `EXPLAIN` to analyze query plans. Add pagination to large result sets.\n00125| - Implement caching strategy: Cache frequently accessed data in Redis with TTL. Use cache-aside pattern: Check cache, miss → fetch from DB → set cache. Define cache key convention: `entity:id`.\n00126| - Use connection pooling: Configure database pool size based on workload. For Prisma: `connection_limit` in database URL. For Redis: `ioredis` with pool. Monitor pool exhaustion.\n00127| - Optimize JSON serialization: Use `fast-json-stringify` with JSON Schema for 2-3x faster serialization. For large responses, use streaming: `res.write()` chunks instead of single `res.json()`.\n00128| - Implement response compression: Use `compression` middleware (gzip, brotli). Configure level vs speed tradeoff. Enable for text responses (JSON, HTML), skip for images, video.\n00129| - Use clustering for CPU utilization: Node.js is single-threaded. Use `cluster` module to spawn workers per CPU core. Or deploy multiple instances behind load balancer (better for containers).\n00130| - Optimize cold starts: Minimize startup work. Lazy load heavy dependencies. Use `import()` for conditional imports. For serverless (AWS Lambda), reduce bundle size, use provisioned concurrency.\n00131| - Implement request coalescing: Deduplicate concurrent identical requests (e.g., same user requesting same resource multiple times). Use in-memory Map to track pending requests.\n00132| - Use async iterators for streaming large datasets: `async function* fetchUsers() { for (const batch of batches) { yield* batch } }`. Process in chunks to avoid loading entire dataset in memory.\n00133| - Monitor event loop lag: Use `toobusy-js` or custom monitoring: `const start = Date.now(); setImmediate(() => { const lag = Date.now() - start })`. Alert when lag exceeds threshold (indicates blocked event loop).\n00134| - Optimize Docker images: Use multi-stage builds. Use alpine base image. Copy only production dependencies: `pnpm install --prod`. Remove dev dependencies and cache. Use `.dockerignore`.\n00135| \n00136| ## Dependencies\n00137| \n00138| - Minimize dependencies: Each adds bundle size, security risk, maintenance burden. Evaluate necessity before adding. Implement simple utilities instead of adding library (e.g., retry logic vs full library).\n00139| - Audit dependencies before adding: Check npm downloads, GitHub stars, last update date, open issues, security advisories. Use `npx socket npm install <package>` for security analysis. Avoid packages with install scripts.\n00140| - Pin exact versions in package.json for applications: Use `\"fastify\": \"5.2.0\"` not `\"^5.2.0\"`. Prevents unexpected breakages in production. Use Renovate or Dependabot for automated updates with testing.\n00141| - Prefer well-maintained, popular packages with TypeScript support. Check for `@types/*` packages or built-in types. Avoid packages requiring manual type definitions.\n00142| - Use workspace dependencies in monorepos: Define in `[workspace.dependencies]` in root package.json. Use `workspace:*` for internal packages. Ensures consistent versions across services.\n00143| - Avoid mixing ESM and CJS dependencies when possible. Prefer pure ESM packages for modern Node.js. Check `package.json` for `\"type\": \"module\"` and `\"exports\"` field.\n00144| - Replace heavy dependencies with lighter alternatives: Use `pino` over `winston`, `ky` over `axios`, `postgres` over `pg` + `pg-promise`. Check bundle size impact.\n00145| - Keep dependencies updated: Run `pnpm update` monthly. Review changelogs before major updates. Test thoroughly. Use `npm-check-updates` for bulk updates: `npx ncu -u`.\n00146| - Remove unused dependencies: Run `depcheck` to find unused deps. Remove `devDependencies` not used in scripts. Check for duplicate packages: `pnpm list --depth=Infinity | grep <package>`.\n00147| - Lock dependency versions with `pnpm-lock.yaml`. Commit to git. Use `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in CI/production to ensure reproducible builds. Never use `npm update` without testing.\n00148| \n00149| ## Documentation\n00150| \n00151| - Write TSDoc comments for exported functions, classes, types: `/** Creates a new user. @param dto - User creation data. @returns Created user with generated ID. @throws {ValidationError} When email is invalid. @example \\`\\`\\`ts\\nawait createUser({ email: 'user@example.com', name: 'John' })\\n\\`\\`\\` */`.\n00152| - Document API endpoints with OpenAPI/Swagger: Use `@fastify/swagger` or `swagger-jsdoc`.
